candidates.name: Donald Norcross
candidates.occupation: Member, US House of Representatives, Retired Electrician
candidates.background: Born and raised in South Jersey, Donald Norcross began his career in organized labor in 1979, working as an IBEW electrical apprentice. He rose through the ranks of the International Brotherhood of Electrical Workers to become a business agent for Local 351. He is a former president of the Southern New Jersey Building Trades Council and served as president of the Southern New Jersey AFL-CIO Central Labor Council for 16 years. Donald raised his son as a single father and knows the struggles families are facing.

promises.question: What is your top issue?
promises.answer: I believe the top issue facing our country is centered around jobs, affordability and the price to live in this country. I have sponsored a bill to raise the minimum wage to $20 per hour, and I have supported efforts to go beyond that. It is time that we take the necessary steps to ensure that all Americans are able to earn a dignified wage for their work.

promises.question: How would you improve the economy and make the cost of living (groceries, housing, energy, etc.) more affordable?
promises.answer: Currently, prices are too high and the Trump Tariff Tax has raised prices by 15% on all Americans. Families cannot afford to put gas in their car, food on the table, and pay their bills. We must stop foreign wars of choice, and we need to focus on lowering the costs of everyday goods domestically. We must ensure we have the supply chains in place across multiple industries so we are not reliant on foreign countries for our goods.

promises.question: What is your plan to make healthcare more affordable and accessible?
promises.answer: I have long supported efforts to bring down the cost of healthcare. Everyone deserves to have access to affordable healthcare. I have supported efforts to bring down the cost of prescription drugs and giving Medicare the ability to negotiate prices. We must do more, and I support efforts that will ensure Americans have affordable access to quality healthcare.

promises.question: Do you support the war in Iran and federal defense spending? If not, what would you change?
promises.answer: There is little doubt of the dangers that the Iranian regime posed, but there are serious questions as to why now, what is the end goal, and what is our plan in this conflict. Also, there are serious concerns that it is Congress who declares war, not the President. We are in need of real answers and until we get clarity on how this conflict is to proceed, I would not support supplemental funding to continue to conflict longer.

promises.question: What are your thoughts about current immigration enforcement policies and what, if anything, would you do differently?
promises.answer: I have serious concerns about how ICE has been deployed across American cities, sent in to terrorize families and children. Locally, in Lindenwold we saw this very thing unfold, with school children running scared. This is not who we are am Americans, and it is not who we can ever become. I believe in real immigration reform, with a pathway to citizenship for those who have been here and following the laws.

promises.question: What changes, if any, should Congress or the president make in elections (requiring voter ID, regulating mail-in voting, etc.)?
promises.answer: Elections are sacred, and the right to vote freely and fairly must never be in question. Over the last few election cycles we have heard continued worries about the fraud in our election systems, but with little to no evidence. There is no doubt we must ensure our elections are fair, and that only US citizens should be allowed to vote, but that does not include sweeping regulations that would alienate married women, or the millions of Americans who do not have the requisite photo ID or passport.

candidates.name: Damon M. Galdo
candidates.background: : Galdo’s website states: I am not a career politician. I am a working husband, father and tradesman who believes that South Jersey deserves better than what we have been given. Throughout my life, I have worked in construction and the trades, building real projects and earning a living just like most families in this district. I understand the importance of hard work and taking responsibility. I know what it means to balance a household budget, face rising costs and worry about the future that our children will inherit. After my last run for Congress I did not walk away. I listened. I learned. And I built something of my own. I started Americas Pulse Network and the Jersey Sure podcast because too many important conversations were being ignored or controlled. I am running for Congress again because South Jersey needs a representative who understands real work, real costs and real consequences.

promises.question: On the economy and making the cost of living more affordable
promises.answer: : Galdo’s website states his priorities are to reduce unnecessary federal spending; support affordable, reliable American energy; encourage economic growth and cut burdensome regulations.

promises.question: On health care affordability and accessibility
promises.answer: : Galdo’s website states he supports greater price transparency, expanding access to Health Savings Accounts, encouraging competition to lower costs, protecting patients with preexisting conditions and making prescription medications more affordable.

promises.question: On the war with Iran and federal defense policy
promises.answer: : WHYY’s voter guide reported that Galdo said he supports Israel’s right to exist and defend itself and he supports “efforts to prevent Iran and terrorist organizations from threatening Israel, the United States or our allies … I believe civilian lives matter and that lasting peace and stability should remain the objective.” Galdo further told WHYY that he supports military action in Iran, but he is against putting American troops on the ground. He would prefer the use of “economic pressure, sanctions, diplomatic leverage and, where necessary, measures such as a blockade to prevent Iran from obtaining a nuclear weaponerests.”

promises.question: On immigration enforcement
promises.answer: : Galdo’s website states he supports secure borders, enforcing existing immigration laws and strengthening cooperation between federal and local law enforcement.

promises.question: On elections and voting
promises.answer: : Galdo’s website states he supports requiring proof of citizenship to vote in federal elections, voter ID, improving the accuracy of voter rolls and strengthening mail-in ballot security.

The Gloucester County communities are Clayton, Elk, Franklin, Greenwich, Harrison, Logan, Newfield, South Harrison, Swedesboro, Woolwich and part of East Greenwich. The Ocean County municipalities are Barnegat Light, Barnegat, Beach Haven, Eagleswood, Harvey Cedars, Little Egg Harbor, Long Beach, Ocean Township, Ship Bottom, Stafford, Surf City, Tuckerton and parts of Berkeley and Lacey.

candidates.name: Jeff Van Drew
candidates.background: Van Drew’s House website states: He is in his 4th term. Before getting elected to Congress, Congressman Van Drew previously served three terms in the New Jersey General Assembly and four terms in the New Jersey State Senate. Congressman Van Drew received his B.S. degree from Rutgers University and his D.M.D. degree from Fairleigh Dickinson University. He recently retired after owning and operating a dentistry practice for 30 years in South Jersey. He and his wife have two children and two grandchildren. Congressman Van Drew is a member of the House Judiciary Committee and the Transportation and Infrastructure Committee.

promises.question: On the economy and making the cost of living more affordable
promises.answer: : Van Drew discusses energy costs on his campaign website, saying he supports “moving into the design phase for new nuclear power at Salem and reinstating generation at Oyster Creek.” He also supports investing in new natural gas plants to maintain energy reliability and affordability.

promises.question: On healthcare affordability and accessibility
promises.answer: : Van Drew says he supported President Trump’s plan to lower prices on some medications.

promises.question: On the war in Iran and federal defense spending
promises.answer: : Van Drew consistently has supported continuing the U.S. war in Iran. As recently as Sept. 16 he voted against a resolution directing Trump to stop the war or get congressional approval to continue it. He voted in July for the 2027 fiscal year National Defense Authorization Act, which would authorize $1.15 trillion in military programs.

promises.question: On immigration enforcement
promises.answer: : Van Drew’s campaign website states he “ fully supports President Trump’s ongoing efforts to secure our border and expedite the deportation of criminal illegal aliens from our shores.” He also voted for a $165 billion border security package, including funds to complete the southern border wall and additional money to the Department of Homeland Security for its deportation efforts. He also defended the Delaney Hall detention center in Newark, saying the facility adheres to proper standards.

promises.question: On elections and voting
promises.answer: : Van Drew voted for the Trump-backed SAVE Act that would make a number of voting changes, including a requirement of proof of U.S. citizenship to register to vote, a mandate that states check citizenship status against a federal database and allowing for criminal penalties for election officials who register non-citizens to vote.

candidates.name: Ramon Mora Jr.
candidates.background: Personal: Vineland born and Raised. Raised in low-income Section 8 housing. Where I grew up often gave pause to adults when I was young. Kids from my neighborhood were looked at as less-than and incapable of achieving or automatically up to no good because of local gangs. After Surviving my childhood and homelessness through brutal winters, I managed to graduate High-school, and then Nursing School in unstable Housing. I have since fought through a back injury that left me functionally disabled to ultimately where I am today. Professional: Prior leadership roles nearly every job held, Nursing Tech, Nursing School Graduate.

promises.question: What is your top issue?
promises.answer: My top issue is affordability hands down. I have lived a life of unaffordability of basic needs. I was homeless as a teen with nothing to my name. I know what the affordability crisis the people are struggling with because I am not just FOR the people but OF the people. Life should be more than paying bills for essential needs. The people deserve to live a life not JUST work a life for a billionaire company so that THEIR executives can live THEIR lives. I have novel plans to target the affordability of our basic needs of life so that way people can not just feel like they are in survival mode but so they can afford to do more in life like starting a family and having a place to call their own. Affordability is my top issue.

promises.question: How would you improve the economy and make the cost of living (groceries, housing, energy, etc.) more affordable?
promises.answer: Improve the economy by putting workers rights, safeguards, and opportunities at the forefront. When the workers are well off our economy thrives in all sectors as people have more expendable income to live life not just work one. Address the massive unemployment looming as AI Hyperscale Data centers come for our jobs. My Grocery and housing policies fight corporate monopoly practices and puts real competition in the market that the citizens of America can have real financial stake in and dramatically benefit from. Energy Cost affordability will be achieved by diverting waste fraud and abuse of taxpayer funds and military overspending. Instead of investing in a war machine we build out our infrastructure in ways we have not seen in decades

promises.question: What is your plan to make healthcare more affordable and accessible?
promises.answer: Advance a Medicare for all/Single Payer system where we can get rid of the billions of dollars being wasted on middlemen insurance companies and focus that money on building out a robust medical industry where we can put American’s Health First and not profits of an insurance company first. I would also untie health insurance to employment. Investing in our country’s health is one of the most patriotic actions we can do, it’s also good for business and the longevity of a society when the people of a country are taken care of. In this kind of system people would not have to worry about co-pays, deductibles, monthly premiums, all just to be delayed or denied care.

promises.question: Do you support the war in Iran and federal defense spending? If not, what would you change?
promises.answer: I do not support Israel’s war in Iran and our involvement in fighting their war. We do not have a federal defense expenditure, we have a federal offense expenditure and that has to change. We waste trillions on war, building bombs, overthrowing countries, blowing up children, and destroying countries in the name of profit. We could be doing so much more for everyone in America if we redirected even a fraction of that spending to the benefit of the people to lower their cost of living and improve their quality of life. I would redirect funding to American Defense and American Citizen Investment.

promises.question: What are your thoughts about current immigration enforcement policies and what, if anything, would you do differently?
promises.answer: They are terrible to put it kindly. We have removed our humanity and walked away from the values that made America, America. We should focus on targeting a person not a people which is not what is happening. Not only that but we should be going after true threats, not the individual who has been here for decades and in everyway except paper, an American. I would Abolish ICE, Prosecute those responsible for Constitutional violations, and Replace with The American Defense Unit (ADU). We need security but we need a full reset because of this administration’s hiring practices and policies.

promises.question: What changes, if any, should Congress or the president make in elections (requiring voter ID, regulating mail-in voting, etc.)?
promises.answer: The president should have no control over elections. Despite overwhelming evidence by left, right, and unbiased reporting that election fraud is not a real concern, A large portion of our country wants more security. I am all for making our elections more secure and transparent. I would sign on to requiring ID. HOWEVER and big however, the government needs to be 100% responsible for providing all documentation at no cost to citizens, provide documentation/ID’s with haste and efficiently, and do so in a 5-10 year transition period to make sure we can adequately provide the documentations without disenfranchising voters or creating obstacles to voting. I would like to see Voting be made easier, secure and well protected for the voter.

candidates.name: Herb Conaway
candidates.occupation: U.S Congressman and Internal Medicine Physician
candidates.background: Dr. Conaway began his career serving in the U.S. Air Force as a Captain in the Medical Corps. During his four years of service, he worked as a general medical officer and advanced to assistant director of his primary care clinic. After completing his internal medicine residency, Dr. Conaway practiced in primary care settings before transitioning to academia. He became a clinical professor at an inner-city community hospital, mentoring and teaching the next generation of physicians. Dr. Conaway also served as an Assemblyman in the New Jersey Legislature for 25 years where he served on the Health, Budget and Military and Veterans Affairs Committees.

promises.question: What is your top issue?
promises.answer: The cost of living and economic security. Too many Americans are working hard and still struggling to afford groceries, housing, energy, health care, and other basic necessities. I believe the federal government should focus on policies that lower costs, increase economic opportunity, and ensure that working families can get ahead.

promises.question: How would you improve the economy and make the cost of living (groceries, housing, energy, etc.) more affordable?
promises.answer: I would focus on policies that directly reduce the costs families face every day while strengthening long-term economic security. That means increasing housing supply and affordability, lowering energy and health care costs, protecting consumers from corporate price increases and anti-competitive practices, and investing in good-paying jobs and infrastructure. The federal government should be focused on making it easier for working people to afford the basics.

promises.question: What is your plan to make healthcare more affordable and accessible?
promises.answer: We need to make health care more affordable while ensuring people can access the care they need. One immediate priority is addressing the high cost of prescription drugs. Americans should not have to choose between paying for lifesaving medications and paying their other bills. Congress should strengthen prescription drug price negotiation, increase transparency and accountability across the pharmaceutical supply chain, and crack down on practices that drive up costs for patients.

promises.question: Do you support the war in Iran and federal defense spending? If not, what would you change?
promises.answer: I do not support the United States engaging in a war with Iran without congressional authorization. Decisions to send American service members into sustained hostilities should be made consistent with the Constitution and the War Powers Resolution, with Congress exercising its constitutional responsibility over the use of military force. I also believe defense spending should be subject to rigorous oversight to ensure taxpayer dollars are being used effectively and that our national security investments reflect genuine threats and strategic priorities.

promises.question: What are your thoughts about current immigration enforcement policies and what, if anything, would you do differently?
promises.answer: Our immigration system should be secure, orderly, and consistent with our constitutional values and due process. Everyone in the United States is entitled to the protections of the Constitution, and immigration enforcement should be conducted with transparency, accountability, and respect for human dignity. I would support comprehensive immigration reform that strengthens our borders, improves our immigration courts and enforcement systems, protects families and communities, and creates a fair and workable path to legal status and citizenship for those who qualify.

promises.question: What changes, if any, should Congress or the president make in elections (requiring voter ID, regulating mail-in voting, etc.)?
promises.answer: Our priority should be ensuring that every eligible voter can cast a ballot and that every lawful vote is accurately counted. Rather than imposing unnecessary barriers to voting, I would focus on investing in the local election officials and municipalities responsible for administering elections, upgrading election infrastructure, strengthening election security, and ensuring that poll workers have the resources and training they need. Our elections should be secure, accessible, transparent, and administered consistently and professionally.

candidates.name: Michael McGuire
candidates.occupation: Family Law Attorney and Navy Reservist
candidates.background: I am a Marine veteran, retired NYPD officer, 9/11 first responder, and current Naval Reservist. My life has been defined by a single mission: protecting the innocent and defending the rule of law. Beyond the front lines, I hold an MBA in Accounting and am a practicing attorney. Having prepared thousands of tax returns for local families and small businesses, I have a direct, technical understanding of how government waste and bad tax policy drain our community. I’m running for Congress to bring Marine-strength leadership to the fight for our economy and our safety. I am ready to stand in the gap for the residents of NJ-03 and ensure our government finally puts American families first.

promises.question: What is your top issue?
promises.answer: The top issue facing NJ-03 is the affordability crisis. New Jersey families are being suffocated by the skyrocketing cost of groceries, energy, and housing. This is a direct result of reckless federal spending and policies that have devalued our currency and destroyed the middle-class dream. My top priority is to restore economic sanity through Marine-strength accountability. We must stop the out-of-control spending, unleash American energy dominance to lower utility bills, and deliver real tax relief to the people who earn it. I am committed to fighting the inflation-fueling mandates of the current administration and making NJ-03 a place where families and seniors can actually afford to live and thrive again.

promises.question: How would you improve the economy and make the cost of living (groceries, housing, energy, etc.) more affordable?
promises.answer: We must address the root causes of inflation: government waste and energy dependency. First, I will fight to claw back unspent “slush funds” and audit every federal agency to eliminate the bloat. Second, we must unleash American energy dominance by expanding domestic drilling and nuclear power. This lowers costs at the pump and in our homes, immediately easing the burden on New Jersey commuters. Third, we need to cut the red tape and regulations that stifle small businesses and drive up the cost of housing construction. By restoring a competitive, market-driven economy and ending the high-tax, high-regulation status quo in Washington, we can stop the “Suburban Squeeze” and bring real, lasting relief to every kitchen table in this district.

promises.question: What is your plan to make healthcare more affordable and accessible?
promises.answer: Healthcare should be driven by patients and doctors. To lower costs, I support radical price transparency and real market competition. Patients deserve to know the price of a procedure upfront, allowing them to shop for the best value. We must protect the promise of Medicare and Medicaid for our seniors by cutting the administrative waste and fraud that threaten their solvency. I will oppose any government takeover that would destroy private options and lead to rationing. Instead, I support policies that allow for portable health insurance across state lines, lower prescription drug costs through increased competition, and prioritize the doctor-patient relationship over the demands of insurance companies and federal mandates.

promises.question: Do you support the war in Iran and federal defense spending? If not, what would you change?
promises.answer: I believe in “Peace through Strength.” The recent decisive strikes against Iran are about restoring American deterrence and finishing a threat. Iran is the head of the snake, and by applying maximum pressure, we protect our allies like Israel and stabilize the region. Strong leadership prevents conflict by making it clear to our adversaries that aggression has a price. This is about global stability and sending a message to every hostile actor that the era of American weakness is over. On spending, we must modernize for 21st-century threats like China while cutting the administrative bloat at the Pentagon. My mission is Marine-strength accountability: a dominant military that ensures peace through overwhelming readiness.

promises.question: What are your thoughts about current immigration enforcement policies and what, if anything, would you do differently?
promises.answer: The Biden border crisis was a total failure of leadership that endangers our national security to this day. Without a border, we don’t have a country. Illegal immigration depresses wages and strains local resources here in New Jersey. We must enforce the laws on the books and ensure our sovereignty is never compromised. This means putting American citizens and legal residents first, starting with a sealed border and an end to the current chaos.

promises.question: What changes, if any, should Congress or the president make in elections (requiring voter ID, regulating mail-in voting, etc.)?
promises.answer: Restoring trust in our elections is essential. I support common-sense measures to ensure that every legal vote counts and that it is “easy to vote, but hard to cheat.” We must also implement strict, transparent signature verification for all mail-in ballots and ensure voter rolls are regularly cleaned of ineligible or deceased individuals. While election administration is primarily a state responsibility, I will oppose federal takeovers that undermine local control. We need clear, enforceable security standards to protect the integrity of the ballot box and ensure that all New Jerseyans can have absolute confidence in the results of our elections.

candidates.name: Steven Welzer
candidates.background: Steven Welzer has been a Green movement activist for over thirty years. He was a founding member of the Green Party of New Jersey in 1997 and he served on the Steering Committee of the Green Party of the United States in 2012. A lifelong resident of New Jersey, Steve lives in East Windsor with his wife and granddaughters. He holds a Master’s degree in Economics from Rutgers University, is retired from a State of New Jersey position in Information Technology, currently serves on the editorial board of the New Green Horizons webzine and is actively working to establish an ecovillage in nearby Kimberton, PA. Steve was the Green Party candidate for Governor of New Jersey in 2013.

promises.question: What is your top issue?
promises.answer: We need to foster electoral system reform. The number of Americans who feel that neither establishment party represents them is at a record high, but the Republicans and Democrats systematically concentrate power in the hands of their wealthy donors. They effectively lock out many of us from our place at the decision-making table. If 20% of the voters support the distinctive ideology of the Green Party, then they should be able to have 20% of the representation in the legislature! So we need to revive our democracy with a full spectrum of reforms including: ranked-choice voting, proportional representation, and public financing of elections. With more voices and more choices in the system, voters could enjoy full multi-party democracy!

promises.question: How would you improve the economy and make the cost of living (groceries, housing, energy, etc.) more affordable?
promises.answer: To strengthen fair competition and economic democracy, monopolies should be broken up, corporate stock buybacks should be prohibited, and global fair trade agreements should be established to protect workers and communities. And I advocate: – raising the federal minimum wage from $7.25 to $25 an hour and indexing future increases to inflation; – supporting the development and growth of worker-owned cooperatives as a model of democratic ownership; – a renter’s “bill of rights” that protects people and small businesses; – major public housing investment with a goal to make 60% of the market high-quality, income-based units i.e. social housing; – empower non-profits like community land trusts to provide housing at affordable rates.

promises.question: What is your plan to make healthcare more affordable and accessible?
promises.answer: I advocate a publicly funded “Medicare for All” healthcare insurance program, administered at the state and local levels, with comprehensive lifetime benefits, including: – dental, vision, mental health care, substance abuse treatment, medication and long-term care coverage; – cost controls via streamlined administration and bulk purchases of drugs and medical equipment; – portability of coverage; – publicly negotiated prices of medications; – funding of clinics and hospitals in medical deserts. – establishment of national, state, and local health policy boards consisting of health consumers and providers to oversee and evaluate the performance of the system, ensure access to care, and help determine research priorities.

promises.question: Do you support the war in Iran and federal defense spending? If not, what would you change?
promises.answer: The war in Iran is a tragic mistake, reflective of our country’s prioritization of militarism rather than diplomacy. Such miscalculations are making the United States a pariah nation! Our defense budget has increased out of all proportion to any military threat. It could be cut in half and still be fully adequate. We should gradually phase out all foreign military bases not specifically functioning under a U.N. resolution to keep peace. Bring home most of our troops stationed abroad! Also: the U.S. is the largest arms seller and dealer in the world. We should prohibit all arms sales to foreign nations and likewise prohibit grants to belligerent and undemocratic nations unless the money is targeted for domestic, non-military needs.

promises.question: What are your thoughts about current immigration enforcement policies and what, if anything, would you do differently?
promises.answer: I would launch investigations into conditions in detention centers under independent public oversight, strict enforcement of open records laws, and regular reporting on facility conditions: – replace internal agency reviews with mandatory checks by external public health and human rights bodies; – require timely public reporting on medical care, mental health services, and safety incidents inside every facility; – prevent individuals from going missing in the system by maintaining updated, public locational databases accessible to legal teams and families. Meanwhile, all persons fleeing political, racial, religious, or other types of persecution must be welcomed and granted permanent resident status and a pathway to citizenship.

promises.question: What changes, if any, should Congress or the president make in elections (requiring voter ID, regulating mail-in voting, etc.)?
promises.answer: There’s no evidence of a significant problem re: non-citizens voting and Trump’s proposed SAVE Act is problematic in that it fails to authorize federal funding for the new state responsibilities it would create. But if there’s support for the idea of proof of citizenship in order to be able to register to vote then we should first implement policies related to getting all citizens to be able to have ready access to such proof. A Real ID can be easy to keep in possession and display. But because there can be some challenges meeting that kind of requirement, it should be implemented gradually. After that regime of documentation is in place it won’t be burdensome for citizens to produce such when they go to register to vote.

candidates.name: Ryan Michael Kelly
candidates.occupation: Educator and former federal civil servant
candidates.background: I am an educator, former local elected official, and longtime public servant. I was elected to the Lake Como Borough Council at age 22 and later taught at New Jersey colleges, including Mercer County Community College. For nearly 13 years, I worked at the U.S. Department of Homeland Security’s Office for Civil Rights and Civil Liberties. I also have more than 20 years of volunteer service with Civil Air Patrol. I am continuing my doctoral studies in higher education and live in Hightstown with my wife, Catherine.

promises.question: What is your top issue?
promises.answer: Affordability. Families feel the economy every time they buy groceries, pay rent or a mortgage, open a utility bill, need childcare, or visit a doctor. I want Congress focused on whether people can actually afford to live in the communities they call home. That means lowering everyday costs, raising wages, expanding affordable housing and healthcare, protecting workers, and making sure taxpayer dollars are spent on programs that improve people’s lives.

promises.question: How would you improve the economy and make the cost of living (groceries, housing, energy, etc.) more affordable?
promises.answer: I would start with a simple question: Are working people actually better off? I support targeted tax relief for working families and small businesses, a living wage, stronger union rights, and paid family leave. We need more affordable housing and stronger oversight of utility costs. We should also enforce laws that protect consumers and promote fair competition. Federal investments in infrastructure and clean energy should create good-paying jobs here at home. Congress should cut waste and focus spending on programs that directly help people.

promises.question: What is your plan to make healthcare more affordable and accessible?
promises.answer: I support universal, single-payer healthcare. Healthcare should be a basic guarantee, not something you lose because you change jobs or cannot afford an insurance plan. Coverage should include doctor visits, emergency care, mental healthcare, prescriptions, reproductive healthcare, maternity care, fertility care, and other medically necessary treatment. We should reduce the role of insurance middlemen and put patients and medical professionals first. Every American should have access to healthcare at least as good as the healthcare members of Congress receive.

promises.question: Do you support the war in Iran and federal defense spending? If not, what would you change?
promises.answer: I do not support the war in Iran. Congress, not the president alone, should decide when our country goes to war. Military force should be used to defend our country and people, not for open-ended conflicts without clear goals or congressional approval. I support a strong national defense and keeping our promises to servicemembers, veterans, and military families. But defense spending needs strong oversight. I would cut waste and unnecessary military spending and invest those savings in needs at home, including healthcare, housing, education, and infrastructure.

promises.question: What are your thoughts about current immigration enforcement policies and what, if anything, would you do differently?
promises.answer: Our immigration system needs stronger oversight and more respect for due process and civil rights. I support abolishing ICE and replacing its current structure with a lawful and humane system that protects public safety while respecting constitutional rights. I would restore strong civil rights oversight at DHS, investigate detention conditions, protect legal asylum, refugee, and TPS programs, and oppose turning local police into federal civil immigration officers. We can enforce our laws while still treating every person with dignity.

promises.question: What changes, if any, should Congress or the president make in elections (requiring voter ID, regulating mail-in voting, etc.)?
promises.answer: Voting should be secure, accessible, and easy to understand. I support early voting and secure vote-by-mail, along with reasonable safeguards such as voter verification, signature checks, ballot tracking, and a fair way for voters to fix legitimate mistakes. Election rules should be based on evidence and applied fairly, not changed to help one political party. I also support stronger campaign finance transparency and reforms to reduce the influence of big money in politics. Every eligible voter should be able to vote and have that vote counted accurately.

candidates.name: Christopher H. Smith
candidates.background: : Smith’s congressional website states: Elected in 1980, Smith is currently in his 23rd, two-year term. He serves as a senior member on the Foreign Affairs Committee and as Chairman of its Africa Subcommittee, which has oversight over the continent, with U.S. legislative authority over Africa, along with important State Department bureaus and programs. He has been appointed to serve as both the Co-Chair of the Tom Lantos Human Rights Commission, and as Co-Chair of the bipartisan House/Senate/White House Congressional-Executive Commission on China (CECC). He has also been appointed as a member of the Subcommittee on Western Hemisphere, which includes the regional focus of Central and South America and functional jurisdiction over the bureaus such as the Bureau of Democracy, Human Rights and Labor, which covers his groundbreaking work to fight human trafficking, advance religious freedom and international labor rights. According to the official Congress.gov website run by the Library of Congress, Rep. Smith has authored 50 laws. Smith was born in Rahway and grew up in Iselin. He graduated from Trenton State College, later renamed The College of New Jersey, with a degree in business administration. Smith was Director of Institutional Sales at his family-owned sporting goods company and served as Executive Director of the New Jersey Right to Life Committee.

promises.question: On the economy and making the cost of living more affordable
promises.answer: : In responding to a question on affordability from Patch , Smith noted that he voted for the Working Families Tax Cuts law. It increased the Child Tax Credit to $2,500 per child, instituted no taxes on tips and provided tax relief for seniors.

promises.question: On healthcare affordability and access
promises.answer: : In answering another question from Patch, Smith said he has “worked tirelessly to expand access to affordable health care and improve the delivery of quality health care for all, especially and including those who need it most.” He said he has supported funding for Medicare and Medicaid and expanding coverage to critical therapies through these programs — including Medicare coverage of diabetic shoes and comprehensive planning sessions for patients diagnosed with Alzheimer’s disease and related dementias — above and beyond the fundamental health care covered by both systems. He also sid he is continuing “to work to drive down the costs of prescription drugs for all Americans.” and supported “allowing American patients to purchase drugs through the mail at prices U.S. companies offered overseas and I support the Trump Administration’s Most Favored Nation program pricing on critical drugs, ensuring Americans are not needlessly overcharged for drugs to subsidize drug prices in places such as Europe.” In Medicare, Medicaid and other programs, he said it is “absolutely critical to continue efforts to fight fraud and abuse” to save tax dollars. Smith supported the comprehensive 2025 bill that instituted work and study requirements for Medicaid recipients.

promises.question: On the war in Iran and federal defense spending
promises.answer: : Smith has voted to continue the U.S. war in Iran. As recently as Sept. 16 he voted against a resolution directing Trump to stop the war or get congressional approval to continue it. He voted in July for the 2027 fiscal year National Defense Authorization Act, which would authorize $1.15 trillion in military programs.

promises.question: On immigration enforcement
promises.answer: : Smith voted for a $165 billion border security package, including funds to complete the southern border wall and additional money to the Department of Homeland Security for its deportation efforts.

promises.question: On elections and voting
promises.answer: : Smith voted for the SAVE Act supported by President Trump that would make a number of voting changes, including a requirement of proof of U.S. citizenship to register to vote, a mandate that states check citizenship status against a federal database and allowing for criminal penalties for election officials who register non-citizens to vote.

candidates.name: Rachel Peace
candidates.background: Born and raised in Ocean County, I’m raising my young son in Monmouth County. I’m 33, a single mom, and the founder of Hyperfocused Communications, a small strategic-communications firm serving mission-driven leaders. After fleeing an abusive relationship, I came home to New Jersey and went uninsured for months — sick with a cough I couldn’t afford to treat, buried in collection notices from a single urgent-care visit. My sister Brittany is alive today because Medicaid covered her care. That’s why I’m running. I’ve lived what this district is going through — rising costs, healthcare on the line, families squeezed. I’m not a career politician. I know what federal votes do in real kitchens, because I’ve sat at one of them.

promises.question: What is your top issue?
promises.answer: Healthcare. Specifically: keeping people insured, protecting Medicaid, and ending the squeeze that makes one urgent-care visit a financial crisis. In NJ-4 this isn’t abstract — Chris Smith voted YES on HR1, scored by CBO at $911 billion in Medicaid cuts over ten years. NJDHS estimates 350,000 New Jerseyans are at risk and the state faces a $3.6 billion annual Medicaid hit. That’s hospitals, nursing homes, and home care for our seniors and disabled neighbors. My sister Brittany is stable today because Medicaid covered her care. The same program is the firewall for thousands of NJ-4 families. I’m running to defend it and to push toward universal coverage that doesn’t bankrupt working households.

promises.question: How would you improve the economy and make the cost of living (groceries, housing, energy, etc.) more affordable?
promises.answer: Affordability in NJ-4 is a power problem. A handful of corporations set the price of groceries, energy, prescriptions, and rent — while working families absorb the loss and Washington protects the cartel. My approach: bring down healthcare costs by defending Medicaid and moving toward universal coverage; enforce real antitrust against the food, energy, and pharmaceutical giants squeezing households; rein in Wall Street investors driving up home prices in Ocean and Monmouth; restore the expanded Child Tax Credit; and make the wealthiest pay their fair share so we can finally fund property tax relief and the infrastructure the Shore has been promised for years.

promises.question: What is your plan to make healthcare more affordable and accessible?
promises.answer: My plan has three parts. First, defend what works: Medicaid, Medicare, and the ACA. Chris Smith voted to cut $911 billion from Medicaid; I’ll vote to restore it and to expand Medicare’s drug-price negotiation to every drug, every year. Second, close the coverage gap — a public option that lets anyone buy into Medicare at cost, on the path to universal coverage so no one in NJ-4 goes uninsured the way I did. Third, attack the cost drivers: cap insulin and inhalers, end surprise billing loopholes, ban medical-debt credit reporting, and break up the pharmacy-benefit-manager middlemen driving prices at the counter. Healthcare shouldn’t bankrupt the people who work the hardest.

promises.question: Do you support the war in Iran and federal defense spending? If not, what would you change?
promises.answer: No. I oppose another forever war, and I oppose Congress sleepwalking into one. When Rep. Glenn Ivey moved a unanimous-consent war powers resolution on April 9, Chris Smith was in the chair — he didn’t recognize it and gaveled the session closed. That’s not leadership. Article I gives Congress, not the President, the power to declare war. I’d vote to invoke the War Powers Resolution and require an up-or-down vote before any sustained U.S. military action against Iran. On the Pentagon: it has failed every audit it has ever taken. I’d protect troops, veterans, and Lakehurst-area jobs while cutting contractor waste, ending no-bid bloat, and stopping blank-check funding for wars Congress never authorized.

promises.question: What are your thoughts about current immigration enforcement policies and what, if anything, would you do differently?
promises.answer: Our immigration system is broken on every end — at the border, in our courts, and in our workplaces. I support comprehensive reform: a clear, earned path to citizenship for DREAMers and long-term residents; an asylum process that actually works on a real timeline; and strong, humane border management — not chaotic raids that separate families, terrorize US-citizen children, or strip due process. I’d restore the trafficking-prevention funding Chris Smith voted to cut by 71% in HR1 — you can’t claim to fight trafficking while defunding the office that does it. And I’d crack down on the employers who exploit undocumented labor to undercut NJ wages. Dignity, due process, and competence — not cruelty.

promises.question: What changes, if any, should Congress or the president make in elections (requiring voter ID, regulating mail-in voting, etc.)?
promises.answer: The system is rigged by gerrymandering and money — not by ordinary voters. I’d pass the Freedom to Vote Act and restore the Voting Rights Act after the Supreme Court narrowed it in Louisiana v. Callais. Politicians shouldn’t pick their voters. I support secure, accessible voter ID — issued free of charge so no working family, senior, or veteran is turned away — and protecting mail-in voting with strong signature verification. I support overturning Citizens United and banning corporate PAC money. And on the rot inside Congress itself: ban member stock trading, enforce real ethics rules, and close the lobbyist-to-Capitol-Hill revolving door. New Jerseyans are tired of insiders writing the rules for themselves.

candidates.name: Sean Kirrane
candidates.background: Kirrane’s website states: Kirrane is a lifelong New Jerseyan, entrepreneur, and executive who has spent over twenty years fixing broken systems in healthcare, finance and technology. He has led multi-billion-dollar companies, turned around failing hospitals, built new infrastructure from the ground up and designed frameworks that deliver measurable results. Beyond his professional accomplishments, Sean is a devoted husband and father of two children, ages 17 and 22. He is running for Congress in New Jersey’s 5th District as a socially moderate, fiscally disciplined Republican focused on affordability, national stability, common-sense values and results. He co-founded Cortex-X, a patent-pending AI governance platform. He formerly built and launched Arcadia Health Partners.

promises.question: What is your top issue?
promises.answer: Affordability and government accountability. New Jersey families are paying more for housing, healthcare, groceries, energy and property taxes, yet they’re not seeing better results from government. I’ve spent over 25 years fixing broken systems in finance, healthcare and technology. I’m running for Congress to bring that same discipline to Washington. I’ve developed three legislative proposals addressing healthcare affordability, homeownership and homelessness. We need structural solutions that lower costs, reduce bureaucracy, and deliver measurable results—not more political promises.

promises.question: How would you improve the economy and make the cost of living (groceries, housing, energy, etc.) more affordable?
promises.answer: We need to address the underlying drivers of rising costs rather than simply subsidizing them. My American Citizens’ Primary Residence Mortgage Act would provide temporary interest relief during high-rate periods, expand mortgage options and help restore homeownership affordability. I support restoring the full SALT deduction, reducing taxes, expanding domestic energy production, modernizing our electric grid and removing unnecessary regulations that increase costs for businesses and consumers. We must also encourage competition and eliminate wasteful government spending. Every federal program should face rigorous financial audits and measurable performance standards. The objective is simple: lower household expenses, increase purchasing power and make New Jersey affordable again.

promises.question: What is your plan to make healthcare more affordable and accessible?
promises.answer: I’ve developed the American Citizens’ Health Insurance Act, a comprehensive reform designed to provide universal baseline healthcare coverage while preserving private insurance, physician choice and free-market competition. At its center is the America Plan, administered through a national healthcare government-sponsored enterprise, with private insurers delivering coverage under common standards. The system would establish transparent regional reimbursement rates, simplify billing, eliminate unnecessary administrative layers and establish income-based limits on out-of-pocket expenses. Primary care, preventive services, and mental healthcare would be integral components. We need to redirect money currently consumed by administrative inefficiency back into patient care. My objective is better healthcare at a lower cost, without replacing our healthcare delivery system with government-run medicine.

promises.question: Do you support the war in Iran and federal defense spending? If not, what would you change?
promises.answer: I support a strong national defense, protecting American military personnel, standing with our allies, including Israel, and preventing Iran from acquiring nuclear weapons. However, I do not support an open-ended war without clearly defined objectives, appropriate congressional oversight and a strategy for ending hostilities. Military action must serve identifiable American national security interests, with diplomacy pursued wherever it can produce a durable result. Defense spending is essential, but it must be accountable. I would prioritize military readiness, cybersecurity, intelligence and our service members while demanding rigorous audits of defense procurement and major military programs. A strong military and fiscal responsibility are not mutually exclusive.

promises.question: What are your thoughts about current immigration enforcement policies and what, if anything, would you do differently?
promises.answer: A sovereign nation must control its borders and enforce its immigration laws. I support securing our borders, enforcing lawful removal orders and prioritizing individuals who threaten public safety or national security. At the same time, enforcement must respect constitutional protections, due process and the rule of law. We also need to fix a dysfunctional immigration system that leaves legal applicants and employers navigating unnecessary delays and bureaucracy. I would focus on effective enforcement, accountability and streamlining lawful immigration. The objective should be an immigration system that is secure, fair, predictable and respectful of America’s long history as a nation of immigrants.

promises.question: What changes, if any, should Congress or the president make in elections (requiring voter ID, regulating mail-in voting, etc.)?
promises.answer: Election integrity is fundamental to public confidence in our democracy. I support voter identification, verification of U.S. citizenship for federal voter registration and the principles of the SAVE Act. These safeguards should be implemented in ways that ensure every eligible citizen can obtain the required identification and exercise the right to vote. I also support legitimate vote-by-mail access with appropriate identity verification, ballot tracking, secure chain-of-custody procedures and transparent audits. Election laws should be consistently enforced, and results should be accurate, timely and independently verifiable. Protecting ballot access and ensuring election integrity should be complementary goals, not competing partisan objectives.

candidates.name: Adam Rueda
candidates.background: Hi my name is Adam Rueda, I’m is a 29 year-old First-Generation Bucknell graduate that has worked successfully as a Senior Financial Analyst as well as in Interior Design and Hospitality. I was raised and have lived in Sussex County for 20 years, my parents were raised in Irvington. Two of my grandparents, Maria Jaramillo and Arturo Rueda, immigrated from Ecuador and Colombia and gained U.S. citizenship. I have lived most recently in Morristown, Jersey City and Downtown Brooklyn. I am deeply concerned with human rights, free speech and getting money out of politics. I believe we need to think creatively around solutions that empower everyday Americans. We need to force our government to start working for the people as soon as possible.

promises.question: What is your top issue?
promises.answer: My top issue is the barbarism, neglect and medical abuse that is being overseen by our government within Delaney Hall and Elizabeth Contract Detention Facility, as well as on the streets of our great state. I am in shock and disgust to see lifelong trauma be sewn into children’s minds as their parents are detained right in front of them. We must end for-profit detention in NJ. Deaths at the hands of ICE were up 450% in 2025 from the previous 12-year average. We must end violent and humiliating public abductions of otherwise law-abiding people. We must work to transition from ICE to an immigration system that is built around basic human rights, due process, pathways to citizenship and keeping families together.

promises.question: How would you improve the economy and make the cost of living (groceries, housing, energy, etc.) more affordable?
promises.answer: In general, we need to enforce anti-trust and greatly reduce the presence of monopolistic forces in this country. Ending the Iran War will improve gas prices in the near term. I am very interested in expanding public transit and electric vehicle infrastructure in NJ, as well as incentives for companies that allow employees to work from home. The cost of living is unsustainable for most working families. In Congress, I’ll focus on lowering the costs people face every month like housing, groceries, healthcare, energy and transportation. I’ll work towards making basic housing a human right, strengthening competition to bring down groceries, moving toward universal healthcare, as well as investing in clean energy and accessible public transit.

promises.question: What is your plan to make healthcare more affordable and accessible?
promises.answer: I believe healthcare is a human right. I will fight for universal, comprehensive, compulsory healthcare that guarantees every American access to quality care regardless of income or employment. No American should avoid seeing a doctor, ration medication or face financial ruin because they get sick. I do not believe being a for-profit corporation is compatible with the mission of healthcare. If you want to learn more about a possible system for universal healthcare, read up on Israel’s “Kupot Cholim” healthcare system, which creates a minimum Health Basket required to be available to all citizens, and involves 4 competing, not-for-profit health funds. Israel does a great job of providing safety nets and social services for Israeli citizens.

promises.question: Do you support the war in Iran and federal defense spending? If not, what would you change?
promises.answer: No, I do not support the war of choice on Iran, nor the killings or targeting of innocent civilians in Iran, Palestine or Lebanon. We need to decouple from Israel, a State that has now fully descended into a full-on genocidal, apartheid oppressor here in late-2026. In general, we need to re-route federal “defense” funding away from imperialist conflicts in the Middle East and back towards improving our country here in the United States. We need to end our complicity in genocide, ethnic cleansing and apartheid in Gaza and the West Bank. Since the U.S. has been complicit in, and directly funded, so much of the devastation in Palestine, I believe we should now work with Palestinians on the ground to rebuild democratic and free Palestine.

promises.question: What are your thoughts about current immigration enforcement policies and what, if anything, would you do differently?
promises.answer: I am disappointed at the inhumane treatment of documented and undocumented peoples alike under this Administration. I am shocked at the cruelty of for-profit detention centers. Too many people are losing their lives. The conditions within these ICE facilities are unacceptable, with thousands of detainees suffering medical abuse, physical beatings, sexual abuse and starvation. This is a critical time in our nation’s history. We need to defund Trump’s ICE and build a better immigration system centered in basic human dignity. We need to close Delaney Hall & Elizabeth Contract Detention Facility, and end violent abductions of non-criminals in our streets. We must work to build accessible pathways to citizenship and keep families together.

promises.question: What changes, if any, should Congress or the president make in elections (requiring voter ID, regulating mail-in voting, etc.)?
promises.answer: We should be doing everything we can to boost voter turnout and instill confidence in our democracy and electoral systems. We need new political parties, new brands of politics and new kinds of unbought candidates to all contribute towards a revived democracy. We must, of course, push for electoral reform, ranked-choice voting, publicly-funded elections and other common sense ideas to empower everyday Americans as voters, and as candidates. I think there should be less barriers to vote, not more. I think even undocumented people that have been living here at least a year should be allowed to vote, as they also are subject to the conditions of the political leadership, infrastructure, healthcare system, law enforcement, tax laws, etc.

candidates.name: Frank Pallone Jr.
candidates.background: I represent New Jersey’s 6th District, covering parts of Middlesex and Monmouth Counties. As the Ranking Democrat on the House Energy and Commerce Committee, I help shape national policy on healthcare, consumer protection, energy, telecommunications, and the environment. I played key roles in the Affordable Care Act, lowering drug costs through the Inflation Reduction Act, and crafting the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law. I’ve secured millions every year for local projects supporting infrastructure, education, and public health. A lifelong Long Branch resident, I began my public service on the City Council before serving in the New Jersey Senate.

promises.question: What is your top issue?
promises.answer: My top issue is really twofold – the Trump Administration’s assault on our democratic institutions, the Constitution, and the rule of law and the affordability crisis. Since returning to office, Trump has repeatedly abused executive power for personal gain and pushed harmful policies that hurt working families. Until there is real accountability of this administration under a Democratic Congress, we won’t be able to effectively deal with the affordability crisis because Trump will always be working to find a way to line his pockets. Protecting our democratic institutions also means ensuring we have a government that works for the public instead of one that is only focused on corruption and self-dealing.

promises.question: How would you improve the economy and make the cost of living (groceries, housing, energy, etc.) more affordable?
promises.answer: I will continue my work reversing Trump policies that have done nothing to help working families, and only further enriched his billionaire buddies. We must focus on lowering costs and improving economic stability for families in New Jersey. Simply put, prices have risen because of the harmful tariffs on key trade partners, the illegal war in Iran, cuts to renewable energy projects that would have reduced utility costs, and attacks on programs like the Affordable Care Act and SNAP that millions of Americans rely on. I have fought Trump’s policies through court action, congressional oversight as the top Democrat on my committee, and public pressure campaigns demanding accountability from this lawless administration.

promises.question: What is your plan to make healthcare more affordable and accessible?
promises.answer: The best way to make healthcare more affordable is to reverse Republican cuts to Medicaid and restore the ACA Enhanced Premium Tax Credits. In New Jersey, 350,000 people could lose Medicaid, while thousands more face rising costs because the tax credits expired. I am also a supporter of Medicare For All. No American should be forced to go without coverage because they can’t afford it, or have to make the impossible choice of buying groceries or going to their doctor

promises.question: Do you support the war in Iran and federal defense spending? If not, what would you change?
promises.answer: I oppose the war in Iran. I will continue to vote for the War Powers Resolution to halt Trump’s illegal actions within 30 days unless authorized by Congress. I will continue fighting to end this conflict before it becomes another costly forever war. Trump attacked without a clear strategy or exit plan, risking another quagmire with no real benefit to our communities. Even the Pentagon acknowledged there was no imminent threat to the United States, yet we have already spent billions, lost service members, and seen prices rise. The war has to end now, and I will keep pushing my Republican colleagues to finally grow a backbone and force that to happen.

promises.question: What are your thoughts about current immigration enforcement policies and what, if anything, would you do differently?
promises.answer: The Trump Administration’s immigration policies have been a disaster. We can enforce immigration laws while still treating people humanely and respecting constitutional rights. ICE should not be conducting warrantless arrests, racially profiling, or targeting sensitive locations while operating like a secret police force. Instead of spending billions on detention facilities, we should invest in affordable housing, healthcare, and lowering costs. I support comprehensive immigration reform with a pathway to citizenship for undocumented immigrants who have been here for a period of time, have not gotten in trouble with the law, and have paid their taxes. The President should end his cruel enforcement actions and go after real criminals.

promises.question: What changes, if any, should Congress or the president make in elections (requiring voter ID, regulating mail-in voting, etc.)?
promises.answer: Voting, including mail-in voting, should be accessible to every eligible American citizen. Yet the Trump Administration has repeatedly spread false claims about voter fraud and pushed policies like the SAVE Act that would make it harder for millions of Americans to vote, including married women, military families, rural voters, and survivors of domestic violence. I oppose these barriers and support restoring and strengthening the Voting Rights Act after key protections were stripped away by the Supreme Court. I also support overturning Citizens United to reduce the influence of corporate money in politics and restore faith in our democracy.

candidates.name: Hillary Herzig
candidates.background: I bring more than a decade of federal public service experience spanning national security, immigration, veterans’ services, agriculture, education, financial management, and public administration. I earned a B.A. in Criminal Justice from Florida Atlantic University and pursued graduate coursework in Political Science. My service has included roles with Department of Army – NGIC, Department of Homeland Security – USCIS, Veterans Administration, USDA APHIS, and DoDEA, as well as coordination and liaison work with the NSA. I also served in local government with the Key West Police Department. This diverse experience gives me firsthand knowledge of how government operates and how its decisions impact the people it serves.

promises.question: What is your top issue?
promises.answer: Making New Jersey affordable for working families by lowering the cost of housing, energy, healthcare and everyday necessities while expanding opportunities to build long-term economic security.

promises.question: How would you improve the economy and make the cost of living (groceries, housing, energy, etc.) more affordable?
promises.answer: Protecting homeowners and renters from displacement, challenging corporate consolidation that reduces competition, supporting American and New Jersey farmers and food production, and pursuing an all of the above energy strategy including nuclear, natural gas, and distributed solar to increase reliable supply and lower costs. I also support expanding skilled-trades education and apprenticeships, strengthening small businesses, and rewarding work rather than creating greater dependence on government. A strong economy should allow a working family to afford a home, groceries, utilities, healthcare, and the opportunity to save for the future.

promises.question: What is your plan to make healthcare more affordable and accessible?
promises.answer: I would make healthcare more accessible by expanding patient choice rather than forcing Americans into a one size fits all system. My Health Care for the Future, Not the Past Act would modernize insurance coverage to include evidence based complementary and alternative care alongside conventional medicine. Healthcare reform should increase competition to provide affordability, price transparency and portability while protecting access for people with pre-existing conditions. The goal is simple: affordable healthcare that follows the patient, provides meaningful choices, and puts healthcare decisions back in the hands of patients and their providers.

promises.question: Do you support the war in Iran and federal defense spending? If not, what would you change?
promises.answer: I support a strong national defense, but I do not support prolonged or open ended war with Iran. Congress has the constitutional power to declare war, and any sustained military engagement should require congressional authorization, clear objectives, and accountability to the American people. Defense spending should prioritize our service members, military readiness, homeland defense, cybersecurity, emerging technology, and maintaining a strong deterrent, not wasteful spending or indefinite nation building. America should be strong enough to defend itself while making diplomacy and the prevention of unnecessary wars a national security priority.

promises.question: What are your thoughts about current immigration enforcement policies and what, if anything, would you do differently?
promises.answer: Having worked within our federal immigration system, I believe we can enforce our laws and secure our borders while treating people with dignity and ensuring due process. I support national sovereignty, consistent nationwide standards for detention and oversight. Congress must fix the legal immigration system itself. We need more efficient, accountable processing systems that do not leave families and employers waiting years for decisions. Immigration policy should be firm, fair, humane, and actually workable.

promises.question: What changes, if any, should Congress or the president make in elections (requiring voter ID, regulating mail-in voting, etc.)?
promises.answer: I support common sense election safeguards that make voting accessible while ensuring every lawful vote is protected. Election rules should be transparent, consistently applied, and designed to give voters confidence in the process while protecting every eligible citizen’s right to vote.

candidates.name: Thomas H. Kean Jr.
candidates.background: I am serving in my second term in Congress and am currently serving on the Energy and Commerce and the Foreign Affairs Committees. I am focused on lowering costs for families, improving access to high-quality healthcare, supporting a robust and reliable infrastructure, boosting innovation at home, and helping students reach their top potential. My office has returned $66 million back to residents and has secured $38 million in investments for local projects in our communities. In 2001, I was elected to the NJ Assembly, where I developed a reputation as a bipartisan leader. Two years later, I joined the NJ Senate where I served 14 years as Republican Leader. I reside in Westfield with my wife Rhonda and our two daughters.

promises.question: What is your top issue?
promises.answer: I have made affordability a top priority throughout my time in Congress and will continue fighting to lower the cost of living for families. Hardworking New Jerseyans face some of the highest tax burdens in the country. As a member of the bipartisan SALT Caucus, we provided real relief for every middle-class family in the state. I led the fight to quadruple the SALT deduction cap to $40,000, putting thousands of dollars back into the pockets of homeowners and families. I will continue to support legislation that cuts burdensome red tape for New Jersey businesses to lower operating costs and spur job creation and support common-sense energy, housing, and fiscal policies that lower everyday expenses.

promises.question: How would you improve the economy and make the cost of living (groceries, housing, energy, etc.) more affordable?
promises.answer: In Congress, I am focused on policies that spur innovation, economic growth, and create good-paying jobs. To strengthen our economy and lower the daily cost of living, we must tackle affordability at its source. That starts with providing real tax relief like quadrupling the SALT deduction to ease the burden on homeowners and cutting the red tape on the federal level so businesses can grow and keep groceries and goods affordable. Addressing rising costs also requires an all-of-the-above domestic energy strategy. We must restore American energy independence and become a net exporter again. This will directly drive down costs for fuel and manufacturing, ensuring much needed long-term stability and relief for Americans.

promises.question: What is your plan to make healthcare more affordable and accessible?
promises.answer: I am championing practical solutions that expand access and lower out-of-pocket expenses for New Jerseyans. I voted to safeguard Medicare and Medicaid to ensure vital care remains protected and affordable for all intended beneficiaries, including our seniors, children, and individuals with disabilities. I also introduced the Mental Health Parity Enforcement and Funding Act earlier this year to ensure that insurance plans provide the same level of coverage for mental health and substance-use disorders as they do for physical health by empowering federal oversight to hold these companies accountable and guarantee equitable coverage. I also co-led the bipartisan HELP Copays Act to prevent insurers from driving up prescription drug prices.

promises.question: Do you support the war in Iran and federal defense spending? If not, what would you change?
promises.answer: Ensuring Iran never acquires a nuclear weapon is essential to our national security and economic stability. For decades, Iran has been vocal about their hatred for the US and exported global terrorism – now they are attempting to export nuclear terrorism. I have long fought back against this threat, and America is finally standing up to Iran through the most focused and targeted campaign in decades. By neutralizing their leadership and capabilities without putting American boots on the ground, we strike a decisive blow against their aggression. I remain committed to providing our military with the time, space, and resources necessary to eliminate Iran’s nuclear threat permanently.

promises.question: What are your thoughts about current immigration enforcement policies and what, if anything, would you do differently?
promises.answer: Border security is vital to our national security and the safety of our local communities. Effective immigration policy depends on knowing who is entering our country each day and ensuring that every level of government works together seamlessly with all levels of law enforcement. By prioritizing direct communication and real-time cooperation between federal agencies, local and state law enforcement, and local elected officials, we can maintain strong oversight, uphold the rule of law, and protect the safety and well-being of our neighborhoods.

promises.question: What changes, if any, should Congress or the president make in elections (requiring voter ID, regulating mail-in voting, etc.)?
promises.answer: Protecting the integrity of our elections starts with ensuring that only American citizens cast ballots. Requiring proof of citizenship is the best way to safeguard the voice of every legal voter. This is why I voted for the SAVE Act in Congress. Recent admissions from Governor Sherrill that over 6,600 non-citizens were improperly registered on New Jersey’s voter rolls highlight why these federal safeguards are necessary. Moving forward, we need total transparency to ensure our elections remain fully trusted and fair for every legal voter.

candidates.name: Rebecca Bennett
candidates.occupation: Former Navy helicopter pilot and healthcare leader
candidates.background: I served more than 15 years in uniform as a helicopter pilot, experimental test pilot, aircraft commander, and officer in the Air National Guard. After graduating flight school at the top of my class, I flew the MH-60 Seahawk and became the 18th female Navy test pilot after attending the U.S. Naval Test Pilot School. Using the GI Bill, I earned my MBA from The Wharton School at Penn. After active duty, my husband, a Navy veteran and union member, and I moved to New Jersey to raise our family. I then built a healthcare career focused on expanding access, improving outcomes, and lowering costs through roles at J&J and digital health companies advancing women’s health and patient-centered care.

promises.question: What is your top issue?
promises.answer: We need to hold the Trump Administration accountable while also solving the issues we are all facing in our everyday lives. The current Congress has completely abdicated its responsibility to be an equal branch of government. Right now flipping the House is critical to provide some form of accountability to the current Administration and restore our checks and balances. We also need to tackle our cost of living crisis and address costs for energy, housing, healthcare, childcare, and more.

promises.question: How would you improve the economy and make the cost of living (groceries, housing, energy, etc.) more affordable?
promises.answer: As a mom of two, I understand the challenges of balancing work & family while navigating inflation and rising cost of living. I’m a pragmatic, common sense leader who looks for common ground to work with people to make life better for everyone. I will champion policies in Congress that will help bring down costs for families in New Jersey. I have put out a robust policy platform addressing these issues with concrete solutions: rebeccabennettforcongress.com/priorities On Housing, On Energy, and On Families, and more.

promises.question: What is your plan to make healthcare more affordable and accessible?
promises.answer: When I left the military, I wanted to continue serving by improving people’s lives. I built a healthcare career focused on women’s health, obesity, and gastrointestinal care, working to expand access, improve quality, and lower costs for patients and families. Meanwhile, Tom Kean Jr. supported policies that raised healthcare costs while protecting tax breaks for billionaires. We need to reverse harmful Medicaid cuts, extend ACA subsidies, and ensure working families can afford coverage. We must also achieve true mental health parity so mental healthcare is treated the same as physical healthcare. I support a public option so Americans can keep their current insurance or choose a lower-cost public plan.

promises.question: Do you support the war in Iran and federal defense spending? If not, what would you change?
promises.answer: As a Navy veteran who has spent over a decade serving my country in uniform, the decision to put our servicemembers in harm’s way should never be taken lightly, and should always be made in consultation with Congress. President Trump has brought us into another forever war with no clear objectives or exit strategy, and Tom Kean Jr. has been complicit in allowing him to continue this endless war. In Congress, I will vote to force a vote on War Powers to ensure we look after our brave service members and prevent another endless war in the Middle East.

promises.question: What are your thoughts about current immigration enforcement policies and what, if anything, would you do differently?
promises.answer: I support comprehensive immigration reform that secures our border and provides a path to citizenship for those here. We also must legally codify the status of Dreamers and give them a path to citizenship. Instead this President is deporting people who followed all of the rules and even sending back those who were granted entry into this country because they protected American soldiers aboard. We also need to ensure that agents are held accountable to the law of the land, like any other federal law enforcement agency and no longer allowed to wear masks, go without identification or body cameras, and enter homes without judicial warrants.

promises.question: What changes, if any, should Congress or the president make in elections (requiring voter ID, regulating mail-in voting, etc.)?
promises.answer: The Administration has made quite clear that their plan to win the midterms is to make it harder for Americans to vote. Without control of Congress or the White House we lack the legislative tools to fight back but that doesn’t mean we have to simply allow them to implement this agenda. We must stand together and bring attention to every action they take to make it harder to vote and motivate Americans to get to the polls, no matter what objections or barriers the White House throws up. Once we take power back we then must ensure we pass vital legislation to protect Americans rights and help make it easier for people to vote.
