candidates.name: Rob Menendez
candidates.background: Congressman Rob Menendez was raised in Union City as the grandson of Cuban immigrants and union members and lives in Jersey City with his wife and two children. Before Congress, he served as a Commissioner of the Port Authority of New York and New Jersey, becoming the first Latino from New Jersey and first millennial to serve on the Board. An attorney, Rob previously worked at Lowenstein Sandler LLP. In Congress, Rob serves on the House Energy and Commerce Committee and its Energy, Environment, and Communications and Technology Subcommittees and as Vice Chair of Policy for the Congressional Hispanic Caucus.

promises.question: What is your top issue?
promises.answer: Right now, immigration is the defining fight for the soul of our nation. ICE has stolen parents from their children, kidnapped workers from their jobs, and used our tax dollars to imprison our immigrant neighbors, and the impacts have rippled into our schools, workplaces, local businesses, and every facet of community life. Trump’s militarization of immigration enforcement poses one of the most urgent threats against civil rights and due process we’ve seen in recent decades. Until we build an immigration system that is rooted in justice and dignity – one that keeps families together and recognizes immigrants as vital to the strength and future of America – we cannot claim to be a nation that values freedom, fairness, or the rule of law.

promises.question: How would you improve the economy and make the cost of living (groceries, housing, energy, etc.) more affordable?
promises.answer: I hear it every day at community health centers, small businesses, and across our neighborhoods. Families are working harder than ever, but the affordability crisis forces them to make painful choices and delay life milestones. Our economy faces real challenges, but much of the strain families are facing could be alleviated with policies that prioritize their needs over corporate interests. We need to first reverse the Trump policies that make life more difficult for families and then advance bold solutions that put people first. From increasing housing supply and investing in housing assistance, to lowering prescription drug costs and advancing universal coverage, we can and must build an economy where hard work is enough to get ahead.

promises.question: What is your plan to make healthcare more affordable and accessible?
promises.answer: Access to healthcare is a fundamental human right. But even before Trump’s massive cuts to health funding, the status quo was failing too many families who struggled to access the care and medications they needed. The most immediate and urgent step is to reverse Trump’s cuts that reduced coverage and made services less affordable, including his inhumane cuts to Medicaid and the ACA tax credit. But we must also rethink how Americans access and afford care and consider all paths to get to universal coverage, including expanding public options like Medicare for All. Affordable, accessible healthcare should be the baseline standard, and we can’t stop until it’s the norm for every family.

promises.question: Do you support the war in Iran and federal defense spending? If not, what would you change?
promises.answer: I have been unequivocally opposed to the war in Iran since Trump first initiated military action, and I have taken every opportunity to vote for War Powers Resolutions to end the war. It’s unconscionable that Trump continues to spend billions on a war Americans don’t want while cutting Medicaid, SNAP, and other programs families rely on. Beyond this war, there’s no doubt our defense budget is bloated and inefficient, with far too much money flowing to defense contractors and outdated programs that do little to actually keep Americans safe – all while we underinvest in working families and their healthcare, housing, and infrastructure.

promises.question: What are your thoughts about current immigration enforcement policies and what, if anything, would you do differently?
promises.answer: Trump’s immigration policies are a direct attack on immigrant families, our community, and our core democratic values. Across the country, we’ve seen ICE’s lawlessness and cruelty result in fatalities and widespread violations of civil and due process rights. ICE must be abolished, but we can’t stop there. Our entire immigration system, from our visa system to our border policies, are fundamentally broken. That’s why I’m fighting for structural reform: a path to citizenship, expanded asylum and refugee protections, safeguards for immigrant workers, DACA and TPS protections, an end to private immigrant detention, immigration court reform, and more to ensure a fair system that recognizes the value of immigrants rather than punishes them.

promises.question: What changes, if any, should Congress or the president make in elections (requiring voter ID, regulating mail-in voting, etc.)?
promises.answer: Our democracy only works when every person can participate freely and safely. But discriminatory policies continue to create barriers that silence too many voices, and Trump’s recent efforts to suppress participation have made protecting voting rights even more urgent. That’s why I’m proud to cosponsor the John R. Lewis Voting Rights Advancement Act to restore and strengthen the Voting Rights Act, combat discriminatory state and local policies, expand access to early and mail-in voting, and make voter registration more accessible. We must protect the fundamental right to vote and ensure every voice is heard.

candidates.name: Da’Shone Hughey
candidates.background: Da’shone Hughey is an entrepreneur, technology executive, educator, workforce developer, and author. My career centers on building systems that use technology, education, and workforce development to expand opportunity and improve everyday lives. I am the author of PhD Ready by 18, a vision for transforming education through AI and emerging technology. My Leadership skills have earned me induction into Marquis Who’s Who in America. Former The View co-host Star Jones interviewed me in light of my leadership skills. My International studies shaped my global perspective. My campaign is grounded in “Giving the Government Back to the People”—with an independent, citizen-centered, solutions-driven approach to public service.

promises.question: What is your top issue?
promises.answer: Economic opportunity, affordable housing, workforce development, apprenticeships, small-business growth, AI and technology education, and government accountability. The Hughey Plan seeks to create pathways to good-paying careers while preparing communities for an AI-driven economy. I support second-chance opportunities, skilled-trade training, and expanding access to education. On foreign policy, I advocate strategic independence, diplomacy, protection of civilian life, and reducing reliance on perpetual military solutions. My campaign is grounded in one principle: “Giving the Government Back to the People”—putting citizens, not special interests, at the center of government and bringing a builder’s mindset to public service today.

promises.question: How would you improve the economy and make the cost of living (groceries, housing, energy, etc.) more affordable?
promises.answer: I would cut costs by increasing the supply of housing, reducing unnecessary barriers and delays that make construction more expensive, and using transit-linked development to lower transportation costs. I would expand apprenticeships to increase the skilled workforce and reduce labor shortages that drive up construction and service costs. I would support small businesses and local manufacturing to shorten supply chains and keep more money in our communities. For energy, I would expand reliable American production and innovation to reduce energy costs. I would also challenge corporate practices that unnecessarily increase prices. The goal is simple: lower the cost of housing, food, energy, and everyday life.

promises.question: What is your plan to make healthcare more affordable and accessible?
promises.answer: I would make healthcare more affordable by attacking the costs behind medical bills. I would strengthen Medicare’s ability to negotiate prescription drug prices, increase price transparency, and crack down on unnecessary administrative costs and surprise billing. I would expand primary care, preventive services, telehealth, and community health centers so people can receive care before conditions become expensive emergencies. I would also support greater competition where it can lower prices without sacrificing quality. I will fight to make healthcare a basic economic security—not a financial crisis—so no family has to choose between paying a medical bill, buying groceries, or keeping a roof over their head.

promises.question: Do you support the war in Iran and federal defense spending? If not, what would you change?
promises.answer: No. I do not support war with Iran. My approach is strategic independence: America should be strong enough to protect itself without perpetual wars or dependence on foreign energy and vulnerable supply chains. As a member of Congress, I would use Congress’s constitutional power to authorize or reject military action and control defense spending. I would demand a clear national-security justification before committing American forces and scrutinize defense spending for waste. I would redirect resources toward cybersecurity, American manufacturing, energy independence, and critical technology. Congress must decide when America goes to war—not simply provide a blank check after the fact.

promises.question: What are your thoughts about current immigration enforcement policies and what, if anything, would you do differently?
promises.answer: America needs an immigration system built for the 21st century—not an endless cycle of border crises, deportations, and political gridlock. I would create a “Pathway to Participation” system: secure the border while establishing a transparent process for undocumented immigrants who pass background checks, pay required taxes, work, train, or pursue education to earn measurable progress toward legal status. I would also create a National Immigration Workforce Exchange connecting documented immigrants with verified labor shortages, while strengthening enforcement against trafficking, exploitation, and employers who knowingly violate immigration laws. Secure the border. Enforce the law. Create pathways. Build America.

promises.question: What changes, if any, should Congress or the president make in elections (requiring voter ID, regulating mail-in voting, etc.)?
promises.answer: I am not convinced that major changes to our election system are necessary. Before Congress changes voter ID, mail-in voting, or other election rules, there should be clear evidence that a problem exists and that the proposed change will solve it without unnecessarily making voting harder. I support secure, transparent, and accessible elections, with consistent standards and strong protections against fraud and interference. My position is simple: don’t change the rules for political reasons—change them when the evidence shows change is necessary.

candidates.name: Aristotle Eliopoulos
candidates.background: I am running for Congress because I believe working class families deserve a voice. As the son of immigrants, raised in Jersey City by parents who owned a small business, I learned the value of hard work, faith, family, and community. My Greek heritage, Pontian roots, and commitment to public service shaped who I am. As a teacher and union representative, I have seen the challenges families face every day, from underfunded classrooms and rising costs to barriers facing children with special needs.

promises.question: What is your top issue?
promises.answer: Special needs advocacy is my top policy priority because every child deserves the opportunity to learn, grow and reach their full potential. As an educator, I have seen the challenges families face when navigating special education, healthcare and support services. I want to strengthen resources, accountability and opportunities for individuals with disabilities throughout their lives. I am also deeply focused on affordability for working families. Housing, healthcare, energy, groceries and everyday expenses are putting tremendous pressure on families. Government should help create an economy where working people can afford to raise a family, own a home, build savings and plan for a secure future.

promises.question: How would you improve the economy and make the cost of living (groceries, housing, energy, etc.) more affordable?
promises.answer: Focus on policies that make everyday life more affordable for working families while strengthening long-term economic growth. We need to increase the supply of housing, reduce unnecessary regulations that drive up construction and energy costs, and encourage competition to lower prices. I would support small businesses, skilled trades, workforce development, and investments in infrastructure that create long term good-paying jobs. We should also address rising healthcare and prescription drug costs and help families build savings and achieve homeownership. At the federal level, Congress must confront wasteful spending and our growing national debt.

promises.question: What is your plan to make healthcare more affordable and accessible?
promises.answer: By capping out-of-pocket prescription costs, expanding federal negotiation of high-cost medications, and requiring hospitals and insurers to provide clear, upfront pricing. I would support goals of expanding primary-care and behavioral-health access in communities, including through telehealth and community health centers. I would also push to reduce unnecessary insurance paperwork and administrative costs by expanding standardized billing and electronic prior authorization. Mental health coverage should include timely access to counselors and behavioral-health providers. Finally, I would protect coverage for pre-existing conditions and measure progress through lower premiums, out-of-pocket costs, prescription prices and wait times.

promises.question: Do you support the war in Iran and federal defense spending? If not, what would you change?
promises.answer: I support a strong national defense, but military action should have a clearly defined objective, congressional authorization is required and a plan for protecting American service members and taxpayers. I would support diplomacy and deterrence while maintaining the capability to respond to threats against Americans and our allies. I would not support open-ended military commitments without clear objectives/congressional oversight. On defense spending, I support maintaining military readiness, modernizing equipment, cybersecurity and protecting our service members, while eliminating waste and unnecessary spending.

promises.question: What are your thoughts about current immigration enforcement policies and what, if anything, would you do differently?
promises.answer: I support enforcement of our immigration laws. I would prioritize individuals who pose genuine threats to national security/public safety, while ensuring due process and appropriate judicial oversight for immigration proceedings. I would also support stronger coordination between federal agencies and state and local governments, with clear limits on their respective roles. At the same time, we need to fix the underlying immigration system by increasing resources for asylum and immigration courts, reducing lengthy backlogs, strengthening legal immigration pathways and improving border security and technology. We should enforce the law while treating people with dignity and ensuring enforcement resources are used effectively and responsibly.

promises.question: What changes, if any, should Congress or the president make in elections (requiring voter ID, regulating mail-in voting, etc.)?
promises.answer: I would support reasonable election-security standards that protect both access and public confidence. Congress should establish clear minimum standards for federal elections while allowing states to administer elections. I support voter ID requirements, Mail voting should remain available, with strong identity verification, ballot tracking, signature or equivalent verification, secure chain-of-custody procedures and timely curing of correctable errors. I would also support regular audits, accurate voter rolls, secure voting equipment and transparent reporting of results. The goal should be simple: make voting accessible to eligible citizens while making elections secure, verifiable, and trustworthy.

candidates.name: Craig Honts
candidates.background: Craig Honts joined the Socialist Workers Party in 1971 after protesting against the killing of students at Kent State University who were opposed to the U.S. war in Vietnam. He was won to understanding why working people need to take political power from the capitalist class to put an end to U.S. imperialism’s wars for all time. He supports Cuba’s socialist revolution and visited there to learn more. Honts visited Canada in August to show support for striking unionists there and to discuss why workers on both sides of the border have no interests in supporting either the U.S. or Canadian rulers’ trade wars. He is a factory worker, member of the Bakery Confectionery Tobacco and Grain Millers union and helps build the labor movement.

promises.question: What is your top issue?
promises.answer: I stand with fellow workers resisting the bosses’ attacks on our jobs, wages and working conditions; building unions; opposing the US rulers’ blockade and threats against Cuba; defending Jews from growing attack; and calling for an amnesty for workers in the US without papers. The spreading conflicts between the US rulers and their rivals abroad are marching humanity toward another world war. The road to prevent that is for the working class to replace capitalist rule with a government of our own and to run society for human need, not the bosses’ profits. The Socialist Workers Party is building a party capable of leading millions of workers to make that possible, as part of the fight for a socialist world.

promises.question: How would you improve the economy and make the cost of living (groceries, housing, energy, etc.) more affordable?
promises.answer: The Socialist Workers Party joins workers building solidarity with strikes and union struggles where working people are resisting attacks on wages and conditions—a course that strengthens confidence in our own worth and ability to fight. A union-led fight for a public works program is needed to provide jobs at union-scale wages to build hospitals, childcare centers and other infrastructure — as is a fight for a shorter workweek with no cut in pay. In the face of skyrocketing prices for food, gas, rent we demand automatic cost-of-living increases in union contracts, pensions, social security. Through struggles working people can be won to the need organize independently of the bosses and their twin parties, the Democrats and Republicans.

promises.question: What is your plan to make healthcare more affordable and accessible?
promises.answer: Under capitalism health care is a business to maximize the bosses’ profits—not meet human need. Thousands of nurses are using unions to fight workloads that put patients’ lives at risk and to demand more jobs. These battles show the kind of struggle needed. SWP members join their picket lines, build solidarity. Through our labor, working people create enough wealth to provide government-guaranteed healthcare and pensions as universal social rights of the entire working class. But it will take a change in which class rules to make that possible. The Cuban Revolution made health care universal. Millions of workers and peasants took power from the capitalists and into their own hands, transforming themselves and setting an example worldwide.

promises.question: Do you support the war in Iran and federal defense spending? If not, what would you change?
promises.answer: There are two sharply different wars against Iran. An imperialist war by the U.S. rulers to plunder the oil, gas, and labor of the region, extend their domination and deal blows to their competitors. And a defensive war by Israel to prevent the Jew-hating regime in Tehran from developing nuclear weapons and the missiles to launch them to advance the goal they share with Hamas and Hezbollah of destroying Israel and carrying out another Holocaust. The working class, the oppressed, and the labor movement must rally behind the fight against Jew-hatred and pogroms. – U.S. troops out of the Middle East! – Not one man and not one penny for the U.S. government, its budget, and its war machine. – Defend Israel’s right to exist as a refuge for Jews!

promises.question: What are your thoughts about current immigration enforcement policies and what, if anything, would you do differently?
promises.answer: Democrats and Republicans seek to divide workers by blaming immigrants for the problems caused by the workings of capitalism and forcing workers without papers to live in fear of deportation. A union-led fight for amnesty for all undocumented workers is needed to unify the working class and strengthen our unions. The SWP opposes raids and deportations of immigrant workers. Winning an amnesty would end their second-class status. This is a life-and-death question for the labor movement. We point to the powerful actions of millions of immigrants on May Day in 2006, who marched under the banner ‘We are workers, not criminals!’ SWP members have joined fights by families in New Jersey against attempts to have their loved ones deported.

promises.question: What changes, if any, should Congress or the president make in elections (requiring voter ID, regulating mail-in voting, etc.)?
promises.answer: The 1965 Voting Rights Act barred measures preventing Blacks from voting. It was a product of the Black-led working-class movement that uprooted Jim Crow racial segregation, a conquest has not been reversed. The bosses’ parties, the Democrats and Republicans, are determined to maintain their political monopoly. They raise petitioning requirements to try to keep the SWP off the ballot The big business press severely restricts its coverage of SWP candidates. Workers can never trust parties that defend the bosses’ exploitation of our labor and promote their wars abroad. We need a political party of our own, but we don’t have to start from scratch. The SWP exists, forged over decades in the class struggle. Help us to build it!

Secaucus and part of Kearny in Hudson are in the district. The Passaic County communities are Clifton, Haledon, Hawthorne, North Haledon, Passaic City, Paterson, Pompton Lakes, Prospect Park and part of Wayne.

candidates.name: Nellie Pou
candidates.background: Nellie is a daughter of Paterson and began her career in public service. She served in various key roles for the City of Paterson. Before serving in Congress, she served in both the New Jersey State Assembly and State Senate. Throughout her career, she has been committed to improving the lives of New Jerseyans. From fighting for better schools to more affordable health care, to criminal justice reform – Nellie has been at the forefront of some of New Jersey’s and America’s toughest fights. Nellie is committed to bringing down prices. In Congress, she is standing up for seniors, Social Security, and Medicare. Nellie has dedicated her entire life to the community that raised her, and in Congress she will never forget where she comes from.

promises.question: What is your top issue?
promises.answer: Affordability. I know how hard it is for families right now when every trip to the grocery store and every monthly bill seems to cost more. My number one priority is lowering the high prices that are crushing families across our district. I have consistently fought to end the President’s destructive tariffs that are driving prices up. I’ve voted in support of legislation that will bring down housing prices, increase access to homeownership, decrease energy costs for families, and have supported policies that would target unfair business practices that drive up the price of goods while reaping in millions in profits for big corporations.

promises.question: How would you improve the economy and make the cost of living (groceries, housing, energy, etc.) more affordable?
promises.answer: I would expand access to low-cost power and fund home heating and cooling, and require large energy users to pay their fair share. I would increase funding for LIHEAP and expand program eligibility while at the same time require data centers to pay their fair share of energy costs so families are not stuck footing the bill. I would also put pressure on the DOJ and FTC to be more aggressive in cracking down on corporate price gouging and in breaking up monopolies. I support regulating surveillance pricing that is driving up food prices. I would also terminate the Trump administration tariffs that are driving up housing construction costs.

promises.question: What is your plan to make healthcare more affordable and accessible?
promises.answer: I would restore the ACA premium tax credits, require 12 months of continuous full Medicaid and CHIP benefits coverage for pregnant/postpartum persons and reverse the nearly $200 billion in SNAP cuts. I would also reverse the devastating cuts that were put in place under HR 1 and expand care under Medicare to include coverage for hearing, dental, and vision. I would expand authorities allowing Medicare to negotiate with pharmaceutical companies on prescription drug prices. I would also increase funding for community health centers and work with hospitals to reduce costs for in-patient stays and services. I’d also create federal grants for medical school, and support school loan payments deferments for medical students.

promises.question: Do you support the war in Iran and federal defense spending? If not, what would you change?
promises.answer: I STRONGLY oppose the war in Iran, and have consistently voted to end it every time a War Powers Resolution has come to the House floor. We need to rein in defense spending, and ensure that federal funds that have been appropriated to the Department of Defense be fully accounted for. I would reduce the annual appropriations for military spending that has become bloated during the administration and use the taxpayer dollars that are saved for programs that help constituents struggling in this economy under Trump.

promises.question: What are your thoughts about current immigration enforcement policies and what, if anything, would you do differently?
promises.answer: These policies are discriminatory and lack basic regard for human life. I’ve conducted oversight of Delaney Hall and I believe the facility should be closed down. I’d completely overhaul leadership serving at DHS and ICE and remove any agents who have violated people’s rights. We cannot allow ICE officers to continue their militarized actions in our communities. I’d prohibit ICE from wearing masks, entering towns and sensitive locations, prohibit DHS from removing its vehicle license plates, and mandate body cameras for immigration agents. I’d uphold constitutional rights and ensure detained individuals have access to clean water, edible food, and healthcare and provide free phone service for detainees calling legal counsel and families.

promises.question: What changes, if any, should Congress or the president make in elections (requiring voter ID, regulating mail-in voting, etc.)?
promises.answer: We must fix the current situation following the President’s removal of all the commissioners on the Federal Election Commission. I would depoliticize DHS and increase funding for Election Security Grants to states. I would restore protections under the Voting Rights Act like preclearance that have been gutted by the Supreme Court. I would ensure every eligible voter receives access to the ballot and vital election information and require that all ballots, forms, instructions, and other materials for the electoral process be provided in different languages. I’d continue opposing the SAVE Act, which imposes overly burdensome requirements hindering access to the ballot for eligible voters, particularly for women and those in the military.

candidates.name: Rosie Pino
candidates.occupation: Adult education instructor, Clifton city councilwoman
candidates.background: Rosemary “Rosie” Pino is a Clifton Councilwoman, community leader, nonprofit executive and small business owner. First elected to the Clifton Board of Education in 2013, she became the first Latina elected to the board and, in 2018, the first minority elected to the Clifton City Council. She is the founder of Latino Leaders of Clifton and Executive Director of ECHO (Educated Communities Help Others), organizations focused on civic engagement, youth development and strengthening local communities. A mother and longtime Clifton resident, Rosie has built her career around public service, community partnerships and creating opportunities for families and young people.

promises.question: What is your top issue?
promises.answer: My top issue is to bring people together to find rational solutions to the mounting issues facing the nation and district. All we seem to hear out of Washington is hatred for the other side. The issues of the day are lost in all the white noise. This election should be a referendum on the performance of Washington as a whole. The climate needs to change. Our campaign is about cutting through all this white noise and fighting through all this insanity and hatred and remembering that our country is facing real challenges. Challenges that demand our attention and deserve our collective voices, talents and contributions. Until we realize that, we as a nation are in real trouble.

promises.question: How would you improve the economy and make the cost of living (groceries, housing, energy, etc.) more affordable?
promises.answer: This is actually 2 questions in 1. The best way to improve the economy is to put the money back into the hands of those who make it. The economy works best when there is free movement of cash. Deregulation, lower taxes, no tax on tips, overtime or Social Security. Higher taxes result in letting the government decide how best to spend your money. Cost of living will only decrease when the war in Iran ends, we end corporate greed and price gouging and when elected officials remember they serve the citizens, not lobbyists and special interests.

promises.question: What is your plan to make healthcare more affordable and accessible?
promises.answer: I believe this is one of the biggest areas of self-interest, corporate greed, fraud, waste and abuse in the country today. Accessibility is largely tied to affordability. The current form of government health care does not work and all the government does is insult each other instead of work on driving costs down. One area of regulation I do support is creating caps on what hospitals can charge and what doctors can charge our most vulnerable citizens.

promises.question: Do you support the war in Iran and federal defense spending? If not, what would you change?
promises.answer: My view on the war in Iran is based on the same information you have. Obviously, I do not yet have my security clearance. I have to trust that the people responsible are making the best decisions for the security of our nation. I do feel the effects of it like everyone else does though. Higher gas prices and food costs. I wonder when the last time a member of congress was in a grocery store like I am every week? As to defense spending, the focus should be on ensuring our troops are properly armed and cared for and not supporting other countries. We as a nation need to make sure those who call on us as their ally actually treat us as an ally and keep our interests in mind before they act in their own self-interests.

promises.question: What are your thoughts about current immigration enforcement policies and what, if anything, would you do differently?
promises.answer: The immigration system in this country needs comprehensive reform. We need to build on our strengths, especially at our borders. We need to adopt clear and even-handed policies on how people can enter this country and become productive and proud Americans. Most importantly, immigration reform needs to be bipartisan. Maybe that way, it will be easier for the federal government to receive cooperation from our state partners. The current system has been broken for far too long and I pledge to advocate for new laws and guidelines to allow for proper paths to citizenship. I want to see in place the ability to find the American dream we have prided ourselves on and like so many of our grandparents achieved.

promises.question: What changes, if any, should Congress or the president make in elections (requiring voter ID, regulating mail-in voting, etc.)?
promises.answer: I absolutely support voter ID to protect the integrity of our democracy. The process needs to be efficient and standardized throughout the country. There is absolutely no place for fraud of any kind either in person or by mail. We must guarantee both parties and states are working together in a bipartisan way to ensure ballot security and accurate reporting. What Washington must never forget is that elections are local. Polling places and county clerk offices throughout this country are manned by regular people, not teams of lawyers or lobbyists. They are our neighbors, grandparents, friends, all just trying to do their civic duty. The rules and regulations need to be fair and easily implemented. Washington is simply out of touch.

candidates.name: LaMonica McIver
candidates.background: Born and raised in the Central Ward of Newark, NJ, I have a passion for public service, and began involving myself in politics at only 13. I have an English Literature degree from Bloomfield College and a master’s in educational leadership and policy from Seton Hall University. For many years, I served on the Newark Council, and was its President for the years prior to my terms as Congresswoman. I worked in the educational field, serving within the Montclair and Newark Public Schools. I call upon these experiences in education and governance as I represent NJ-10.

promises.question: What is your top issue?
promises.answer: Across America, but particularly in areas with lower income communities, affordability is impacting families. More and more, people struggle to afford necessities like food, rent, and gas. We face an affordability crisis, and I know that no matter where one comes from, they are suffering because of it. At the core of each of my policies is improving the quality of life for all. We cannot thrive in a nation where we are priced out of groceries or housing. I will not stop fighting to lower costs and increase access to necessities for each family.

promises.question: How would you improve the economy and make the cost of living (groceries, housing, energy, etc.) more affordable?
promises.answer: To combat the worsening economy, I will continue to support legislation that lowers costs for everyday people. During my time as Congresswoman, I introduced countless bills aimed at lowering costs and supporting families. The Summer Meals REACH Act would allow all children access to school meals – even during the summer. The UPLIFT Act would ease the burden of energy costs in households during inflation spikes through a new federal tax credit, saving you money, and the SNAP Benefits Fairness Act would increase eligibility to SNAP benefits, putting money back in your hands. I plan to, if reelected, continue to prioritize legislation that elevates the voices of everyday Americans, ensuring that the cost of living is attainable for all.

promises.question: What is your plan to make healthcare more affordable and accessible?
promises.answer: Regardless of factors like zip code, race, ethnicity, or economic status, every American deserves access to healthcare. Barriers in our healthcare system affect certain communities disproportionately, and I will fight to dismantle this inequity. If reelected, I will continue to advocate for universal healthcare and higher investment in existing and new healthcare infrastructure, particularly in underserved areas. I have been in staunch opposition to budget proposals that cut funding to healthcare affordability programs. The funding for Medicaid, for example, has been cut, increasing the out of pocket costs for all Americans. I pledge to continue to vote against any threat to affordable and accessible healthcare.

promises.question: Do you support the war in Iran and federal defense spending? If not, what would you change?
promises.answer: I strongly oppose the war in Iran, and have fought to decrease federal defense spending. As of August, the Iran war has cost the US more than $38 billion, according to the Congressional Budget Office. I have said that this is a war of choice, and Trump has not followed the framework set out in the Constitution to authorize military action. The war has endangered our service members and threatens civilians in Iran, and we are funding it. I advocate for a peaceful resolution to international disputes and conflicts, and this one is no exception. I will not stand for a war bringing unnecessary costs and violence, and that is not authorized by Congress.

promises.question: What are your thoughts about current immigration enforcement policies and what, if anything, would you do differently?
promises.answer: Our immigration system is broken, and too many individuals have paid the price. Families are unnecessarily separated, the immigration process takes far too long, and federal agencies are pitted against individuals instead of protecting them. As Congresswoman, I have fought for ICE to be shut down, and for the strict oversight of the immigration enforcement process. I introduced the No Delay for Immigration Oversight Act to protect the oversight Trump has attacked. I have visited Delaney Hall, a for-profit immigration center in NJ-10, on many occasions to meet with detainees and report on its conditions. America is built from the work of immigrants, and I will not stop fighting for a just and dignified immigration system.

promises.question: What changes, if any, should Congress or the president make in elections (requiring voter ID, regulating mail-in voting, etc.)?
promises.answer: We are witnessing an attack on our right to vote by Republicans in Congress, and access to a fair election is being used as a weapon to weaken our minority communities. A fair, transparent, and trustworthy election process is foundational, and I will fight to uphold this tenet of our government. I will continue to strongly oppose the SAVE Act, which threatens Americans’ rights by requiring individuals to jump through hoops to register and vote.

He was a product of the foster care system, at times living on the streets. Today he is living the American Dream while showing young people that anything can happen if you work hard and follow your dreams. His background and business mindset give him the ability to negotiate and work with others no matter what the issue is and come together to find common ground. For over 20 years he has been involved in the political process. He has been an active member of the Republican Committee of Kenilworth. He has worked on many campaigns and run for multiple positions, including Commissioner, State Senate and Congress. He also was an elected official for the Board of Education in Belleville.

promises.question: On the economy and making the cost of living more affordable
promises.answer: : On his campaign website, Bucco states he would fight to end irresponsible spending so people could keep more of their money. He also said he is committed to creating a business-friendly environment that fosters local opportunity and prosperity.

promises.question: On health care affordability and accessibility
promises.answer: : On his campaign website, Bucco addresses mental health reform, stating he would work to ensure people get real support and would not have to struggle alone.

promises.question: On the war with Iran and federal defense policy
promises.answer: : In responding to a more general question from the 2024 voter guide on the role of the U.S. in foreign conflicts, Bucco stated, “Regarding providing aid and support in foreign conflicts such as those in Ukraine and Israel/Gaza, my perspective is that while it’s important to assist our allies, the United States cannot bear the entire burden alone. Persisting in this approach would lead to excessive spending and over taxation of our citizens, ultimately jeopardizing our ability to sustain such assistance.”

promises.question: On immigration enforcement
promises.answer: : In answering the 2024 voter guide, Bucco said “illegal immigration” was a “significant” concern facting the nation.

promises.question: On elections and voting
promises.answer: : Responding to the 2024 voter guide, Bucco stated, “In order to uphold the integrity of elections and facilitate a seamless transition of power, it’s essential to implement voter ID requirements. Additionally, eliminating drop boxes and restricting mail-in ballots to the sick, elderly, and active-duty troops can help maintain transparency. Furthermore, designating election day as a national paid holiday and mandating that companies compensate employees who provide proof of voting would encourage voter turnout.”

candidates.name: Analilia Mejia
candidates.background: : In answering the 2026 special election voter guide, Mejia stated: I’m a mom, grassroots organizer, and nationally recognized policy advocate. Born and raised in New Jersey to immigrant parents, I grew up watching my mom and dad work multiple jobs and still struggle to pay the bills. When my mom got a union job in the city, everything changed, and I’ve dedicated my life to fighting for families like mine. I’ve worked for labor unions as an organizer, led the New Jersey Working Families to win the $15 minimum wage and paid sick days, served as Bernie Sanders’ National Political Director in 2020 and worked in the Biden Labor Department.

promises.question: On the economy and high costs
promises.answer: : In Mejia’s answer to the 2026 special election voter guide, she stated that t he economy is rigged by billionaires, for billionaires, while everyone else fights over scraps. We have to break up monopolies that are price-gouging families, tax billionaires to pay for universal healthcare and childcare, ban hedge funds from bulk-buying homes, raise the minimum wage to $25/hour, provide a federal tax break on the first $40,000 of your income and give workers rights to form a union. When workers have power and big corporations have competition, prices come down. And when families no longer have to stretch their budgets to pay for healthcare and childcare, they have more money in their pockets.

promises.question: On healthcare affordability and availability
promises.answer: : In Mejia’s answer to the 2026 special election voter guide, she stated a desire t o restore ACA subsidies immediately — families can’t wait. Then we must fight for Medicare for All so we have a single-payer system where healthcare is a human right. The current system lets insurance companies and pharmaceutical corporations rake in billions while people ration medications and skip doctor visits.

promises.question: On the Iran War and defense spending
promises.answer: : During an Oct. 26 League of Women Voters Morris Area debate with her opponent, Mejia said, “We have been dragged into an illegal war that is consting you more at the gas pump, and it’s costing you more in every aspect of your life.”

promises.question: On immigration and the current enforcement crackdown
promises.answer: : In Mejia’s answer to the 2026 special election voter guide, she stated that a bolishing ICE was one of her top issues. Democrats in Congress just watch while ICE shoots innocent people in broad daylight. She said she would use every tactic available — from the power of the purse to the bully pulpit — to stop the lawlessness and hold this administration accountable. That includes impeaching Trump, banning insurrectionists from office and prosecuting every single person responsible for the terror ICE is inflicting on our communities.

promises.question: On voting and elections
promises.answer: : In Mejia’s answer to the 2026 special election voter guide, she stated that saving democracy was one of her top issues. In an interview with Briana Vannozzi on NJ Spotlight News with Briana Vannozzi after being sworn into office, Mejia criticized the influence of money in politics, saying “Big money has captured our political system.”

candidates.background: I’m a husband, father of three, Randolph councilman, and former mayor. I’ve spent my career bringing people together and solving problems, both in the private sector and in local government. As mayor and councilman, I’ve worked to keep taxes under control, support our police, and make Randolph a great place to raise a family. I’m running for Congress because Washington needs more leaders who understand that public service is about delivering results, not ideology, for the people you represent.

promises.question: What is your top issue?
promises.answer: Affordability. New Jersey families are doing everything right, working hard, raising their kids, and trying to save for the future, but too many feel like they’re falling further behind. Housing, groceries, utilities, healthcare, and property taxes all cost too much. My priority in Congress will be making it easier to build a middle-class life here again. That means lowering costs, growing our economy, protecting taxpayers, and making sure government works for families instead of making their lives more expensive.

promises.question: How would you improve the economy and make the cost of living (groceries, housing, energy, etc.) more affordable?
promises.answer: I would focus on the costs families actually pay every month. We need more American energy to lower utility and transportation costs, fewer unnecessary regulations that raise the price of housing and doing business, and tax relief that lets families keep more of what they earn. I also support helping first-time homebuyers and making it easier for small businesses to grow and create good-paying jobs. We need more of the money we send from NJ to Washington coming back into the state to help our residents.

promises.question: What is your plan to make healthcare more affordable and accessible?
promises.answer: Healthcare reform should lower costs without taking away the doctors, coverage, or benefits people depend on. I support greater price transparency so patients know what they’re paying, more competition among providers and insurers, removing the power of pharmacy benefit managers, and expanding options for small businesses to provide affordable coverage through AHPs. We should also protect Medicare and reduce seniors’ out-of-pocket costs. I oppose a government takeover of healthcare.

promises.question: Do you support the war in Iran and federal defense spending? If not, what would you change?
promises.answer: Under no circumstances can Iran be allowed to possess a nuclear weapon or the capability to build one. I would always prefer diplomacy to succeed, but if military action is necessary to prevent a nuclear-armed Iran, protect American lives, and defend our allies, I support it. At the same time, I do not support endless wars or putting American troops on the ground without a clear mission and strategy. I support a strong, well-funded military, but Congress must demand accountability and ensure every defense dollar strengthens our national security.

promises.question: What are your thoughts about current immigration enforcement policies and what, if anything, would you do differently?
promises.answer: We are a nation of immigrants and a nation of laws, and those principles are not mutually exclusive. We need to secure the border, enforce our immigration laws, and stop fentanyl, human trafficking, and criminals from entering our country. At the same time, enforcement should be professional, targeted, and accountable. I support better training and de-escalation protocols for ICE and cooperation with state and local law enforcement. We also need Congress to finally fix our broken legal immigration system rather than allowing the problem to continue.

promises.question: What changes, if any, should Congress or the president make in elections (requiring voter ID, regulating mail-in voting, etc.)?
promises.answer: Every eligible American should be able to vote, and every voter should have confidence that our elections are secure, fair, and accurately counted. I support reasonable voter identification requirements that include safeguards ensuring eligible citizens can obtain identification and vote. Mail-in voting should include clear verification, chain-of-custody, and ballot-security standards. Election rules should be transparent and consistently applied.

candidates.name: Alan Bond
candidates.background: : According to the website Chief Investment Officer, Bond had worked as a money manager for a number of firms. In 2001, he was accused of profiting from a financial scheme in which his clients lost more than $57 million. He pled guilty and in 2003, he was sentenced to 12.5 years in federal prison and ordered to pay $12.3 million in restitution. He was released in 2008.

promises.question: On the economy and making the cost of living more affordable
promises.answer: : On his campaign website, Bond states that he supports efforts to build more housing, encourage abundant and reliable American energy, increase competition throughout healthcare, reduce unnecessary regulatory costs, strengthen domestic supply chains, support small businesses and make sure tax policy doesn’t unnecessarily squeeze working and middle-class families.

promises.question: On health care affordability and accessibility
promises.answer: : On his campaign website, Bond calls for an evaluation of the negotiated Medicare drug prices. He also calls for drug-pricing to be patient-centered.

promises.question: On the war with Iran and federal defense policy
promises.answer: : In a statement published on the NJ Globe website last April, Bond wrote, “Sending American troops into combat is one of the most serious votes a member of Congress can make. I would support deployment only when U.S. national security is directly threatened, when objectives are clearly defined, and when diplomacy and sanctions have been exhausted. Our service members deserve leadership that treats that decision with the gravity it requires.”

promises.question: On immigration enforcement
promises.answer: : In his statement published by NJ Globe, Bond wrote, “We need secure borders and a lawful immigration system, but we also need policies that reflect American values. Immigration enforcement should remain a federal responsibility carried out professionally and transparently. Congress should strengthen the legal immigration process, increase immigration court capacity, and ensure enforcement is focused on safety — not fear. Security and dignity can exist together.”

promises.question: On elections and voting
promises.answer: : Bond’s position on electoral reform are unknown.

districts.intro: The 12 th Congressional District encompasses parts of Mercer, Middlesex and Somerset counties and Plainfield in Union County. The Mercer County municipalities are Ewing, Hopewell borough and township, Pennington, Princeton, Trenton and West Windsor. The Middlesex communities are Cranbury, Dunellen, East Brunswick, Helmetta, Jamesburg, Middlesex, Milltown, Monroe, North Brunswick, Plainsboro, South Brunswick, South River, Spotswood and part of Old Bridge. The Somerset municipalities are Bound Brook, Franklin, Manville, Millstone, Montgomery, North Plainfield, Rocky Hill and South Bound Brook and parts of Bridgewater and Hillsborough.

candidates.name: Adam Hamawy
candidates.background: I am a doctor, veteran, and proud father from Jersey. On 9/11, I treated victims in a field hospital at Ground Zero. I served as a combat trauma surgeon in Iraq at the height of the war. One of my patients later became a US Senator – Tammy Duckworth. Since completing my service, I have worked in New Jersey emergency rooms and built my own practice in Princeton. Over the last 30 years, I have volunteered to treat patients in war and disaster zones across the world. In 2024, I went on a medical mission to Gaza, where I was trapped with my colleagues when Israel seized the Rafah Crossing. I refused to leave until all my colleagues were guaranteed safe evacuation. I was honored to be Rep. Bonnie Watson Coleman’s 2025 State of the Union guest.

promises.question: What is your top issue?
promises.answer: Healthcare, not bombs. Every day, I see working families getting crushed by the health insurance industry. Premiums feel like a second mortgage. Treatments are denied while patients are getting sicker. In the richest country the world has ever known, no one should be choosing between rent and medical bills. That’s not a healthcare system – it’s a scam to enrich CEOs. At the same time, I have seen what we actually spend our money on. Over 2 trillion dollars in Iraq and Afghanistan. A bloated Pentagon budget that goes up every year at the same time we are cutting Medicaid. We have our priorities wrong as a country. It is time we invest in our communities instead of giving blank checks to defense contractors and war profiteers.

promises.question: How would you improve the economy and make the cost of living (groceries, housing, energy, etc.) more affordable?
promises.answer: The United States is the wealthiest country in the history of the world, but tens of millions of Americans are struggling to afford rent, childcare, healthcare, and groceries. That is not bad luck. It is the result of deliberate policy choices made by politicians who answer to billionaires and corporations instead of working families. I support large federal investments in clean energy and housing to address rising prices and stimulate our economy. We need to end wars like the one we started in Iran that are driving up gas prices. We need to break up monopolies that are abusing their market power to price gouge consumers. We also need to take care of expensive basic needs like healthcare and childcare.

promises.question: What is your plan to make healthcare more affordable and accessible?
promises.answer: I believe healthcare is a basic human right, not a privilege. As a physician who sees firsthand how insurance companies and the rest of our absurd system fail patients and providers alike, the fight for Medicare for All is personal for me.The root cause of our failing healthcare system is a choice to protect a greedy industry that prioritizes profit over health and well-being. We need universal, single-payer healthcare with no out-of-pocket costs. Crucially, Medicare for All would also expand coverage to include hearing, dental, and vision insurance. I also support empowering Medicare to negotiate prescription drug pricing, breaking up PBMs, fighting hospital consolidation, and cancelling medical debt.

promises.question: Do you support the war in Iran and federal defense spending? If not, what would you change?
promises.answer: I strongly oppose the war in Iran and believe we need to meaningfully reduce the wasteful Pentagon budget. Most Members of Congress never have to face the consequences of the votes they take on foreign policy. As a former U.S. Army combat surgeon who served in Iraq and as a physician who has volunteered on medical missions to warzones all over the world, I have confronted the human cost of decisions made by those in power. For me, foreign policy is not some far off thing – it’s personal. We need to end endless wars and invest in healthcare, not bombs.

promises.question: What are your thoughts about current immigration enforcement policies and what, if anything, would you do differently?
promises.answer: As an immigrant, I take this fight personally. Funded by tens of billions of taxpayer dollars, masked federal agents with military equipment racially profile our neighbors, kidnap them off the street, and shoot and kill them with impunity. Ripping children and grandparents away from their families, subjecting them to inhumane conditions in detention, and sending them to torture prisons in El Salvador is not brave or courageous — it’s cruel and cowardly. I support abolishing and prosecuting ICE. I support building an immigration system that protects civil rights and civil liberties and allows for a fair and orderly process for people to move here.

promises.question: What changes, if any, should Congress or the president make in elections (requiring voter ID, regulating mail-in voting, etc.)?
promises.answer: Money from billionaires and corporations floods our elections and influences our elected officials who should be representing our interests. Our political system is designed for this kind of corruption, not for democracy. The Citizens United decision opened the floodgates to unlimited, anonymous money in our elections. I will fight to establish public financing of elections, mandate full disclosure of dark money donors, and push for a constitutional amendment to make clear that corporations are not people and money is not speech. I will fight to restore and strengthen the Voting Rights Act, pass automatic voter registration, expand early voting and vote by mail, end partisan gerrymandering, and make Election Day a federal holiday.

candidates.name: Gregg Mele
candidates.background: : A Mele campaign website states: Congressional candidate Gregg Mele is a life-long resident of New Jersey who is passionate about restoring liberty and freedom to the state. He comes from humble beginnings – the child of blue-collar parents whose father worked long hours in a bookbinding factory so his family might have a better life. A Montclair State cum laude graduate, Gregg continued his education and eventually graduated cum laude from New York University Law School with his LLM. In between he earned his MS from Stevens Institute of Technology, his MBA from Baruch College of the City University of New York and his JD from New York Law School. He is a prior candidate with statewide name recognition. Gregg has also spent more than a decade teaching graduate-level courses in law, finance, economics and technology at Stevens Institute of Technology and Fairleigh Dickinson University, contributing to a nationally used course textbook.

promises.question: On the economy and making the cost of living more affordable
promises.answer: : Mele’s campaign website states he supports reliable, dispatchable energy generation; nuclear power and natural gas alongside competitive emerging technologies; faster permitting for responsible domestic energy and grid infrastructure and clear disclosure of subsidies, transmission expenses, and other policy-driven costs borne by taxpayers or ratepayers.

promises.question: On health care affordability and accessibility
promises.answer: : Mele’s website states that he supports greater price transparency, more competition, portability, and targeted reforms intended to give patients more information and more choice rather than replacing the current system with a single federal payer.

promises.question: On the war with Iran and federal defense policy
promises.answer: : Mele’s campaign website states that he supports Israel’s right to defend itself and the preservation of a strong U.S.–Israel alliance. Hamas, Hezbollah and Iran-backed terrorism are threats that U.S. policy must address directly.

promises.question: On immigration enforcement
promises.answer: : Mele’s website states that he supports stronger screening at ports of entry, enforcement of immigration law and improvements to legal immigration so applicants who follow the rules are treated fairly and efficiently. He would prioritize dangerous criminals, traffickers, and national-security threats, while respecting human dignity and constitutional protections. He supports law enforcement but believes that those who violate the law should be held accountable.

promises.question: On elections and voting
promises.answer: : Mele’s position on this issue is unknown.

candidates.name: Andres Jinete
candidates.background: I am a 29 year-old tenant organizer from Bound Brook, New Jersey. I am also a management student at Kean University and an aspiring children’s librarian. For the past 10 years, I have worked at several different libraries across the district setting up programming for seniors and families. I led a union drive in one of the largest apartment complexes in Highland Park, demanding transparency for arbitrary up-charges in services and a stop to outrageous rent increases. When unaccountable and reckless ICE agents came into our communities, I also helped build a Rapid Response network across the state to address community needs.

promises.question: What is your top issue?
promises.answer: As a tenant organizer, I think the most urgent issue to address is the unaffordable cost of housing. I would propose a “Renter’s Bill of Rights” modeled on the work of former Seattle councilwoman Kshama Sawant and Workers Strike Back. In addition, advocating for a housing model that mirrors the one in Vienna, Austria in which the majority of units in the market are owned either directly by the government or non-profit Community Land Trusts, would keep housing affordable long-term. I would also promote a Housing First approach that seeks to rapidly house homeless families and individuals without prerequisites, in order to provide shelter and stability as quick as possible. Housing is a human right and we should treat it as such.

promises.question: How would you improve the economy and make the cost of living (groceries, housing, energy, etc.) more affordable?
promises.answer: We live in a financialized casino economy where the needs of everyday Americans are not even a consideration to those at the very top. As household debt soars, families are displaced due to increasing rents, and folks struggle to afford healthcare, the profits for billionaires, and basic necessities like groceries and electricity. We need bold economic programs that create social housing, stabilize rent, provide free healthcare and education and generate the green jobs of the future. If we tax the top 1% of income earners, cut our inflated military budget and enact monetary reform by issuing debt-free money, I believe that would go a long way to improving the economy and making everyday essentials more affordable.

promises.question: What is your plan to make healthcare more affordable and accessible?
promises.answer: We need to force a vote on Medicare for All. We have existing healthcare infrastructure that could be expanded and restructured for the need of all Americans. Medicare has to become a universal single payer system and we need to cut out the middlemen, a.k.a. the insurance companies, that continue to profit off the backs of working people. Paying healthcare providers directly would be cheaper and more ethical.

promises.question: Do you support the war in Iran and federal defense spending? If not, what would you change?
promises.answer: I do not support the pointless and costly war in Iran. In the Persian Gulf, we have seen the U.S. set up military bases in almost all of Iran’s neighboring countries. In the current, unprovoked, US-Israeli aggression against Iran, the bases were used to carry out strikes on schools, hospitals, universities and many other civilian targets; these acts constitute crimes against humanity. We need to stop the expansion of the military-industrial complex that profits from these constant wars and pointless deaths. We have no business having more than 700 military bases around the world, while at home we can’t provide 700 clinics in medical deserts or 700 free universities.

promises.question: What are your thoughts about current immigration enforcement policies and what, if anything, would you do differently?
promises.answer: I believe the current immigration enforcement policies have been a train wreck. We are are seeing rogue ICE agents threaten the civil liberties of immigrants and U.S. citizens. The detention centers lack clean water, provide maggot-infested or expired food, all while cramming in as many people as they can. They pay no mind to women who are pregnant, working people, the elderly or minors who they separate from their parents. We need to demilitarize the immigration system and provide common sense paths to legalization while ensuring due process.

promises.question: What changes, if any, should Congress or the president make in elections (requiring voter ID, regulating mail-in voting, etc.)?
promises.answer: We need to make it easier for people to vote, offering to register them at every possible opportunity when they interact with the government in their daily life, while ensuring that our immigrant neighbors are not automatically registered. In addition, we need to have dedicated divisions within agencies that oversee elections to ensure homeless individuals are registered.

candidates.name: Winston Jordan
candidates.background: I am a U.S. Army veteran running a first-of-its-kind zero-donor campaign. I will govern through a zero-donor incumbency, accepting no money from corporations, PACs, wealthy interests, or individual donors. I will support future Stop Act legislation modeled on H.R. 415 to end forced call-time fundraising that pressures legislators to spend hours calling wealthy donors for campaign money in DCCC call centers instead of serving constituents. In keeping with the Framers’ vision of a U.S. representative, I will serve NJ 12 full time through direct constituent participation, directing federal resources to measurable programs that eliminate poverty in NJ 12, expand healthcare access, and deliver economic security and liberty.

promises.question: What is your top issue?
promises.answer: Eliminate the 10% chronic poverty rate in NJ 12. One in ten residents lives in chronic poverty while the tax code rewards wealth concentration. The framers designed the House to direct federal resources toward solving district problems and securing economic security and liberty for all. For decades, national pledges have functioned as a structural bait and switch, leaving problems unresolved while token earmarks fund ribbon-cutting events that serve re-election campaigns rather than constituents. I will launch at-scale District First pilots including a universal income pilot, healthcare access through VA+, and direct constituent participation in appropriations. These will produce measurable results within a two-year term.

promises.question: How would you improve the economy and make the cost of living (groceries, housing, energy, etc.) more affordable?
promises.answer: I will pursue an NJ 12 economic security pilot centered on a universal income for U.S. citizens. Stable income helps families pay for groceries, rent, utilities, and healthcare while supporting local businesses. I reject national solutions that serve as a bait and switch, leaving district problems unsolved while politicians use meager earmarks for ribbon-cutting photo ops and electoral patronage. I will seek federal funding for district-scale programs that reduce poverty and measure results openly. I also support ending the long tax code advantages that concentrated wealth, strengthening Social Security, and requiring large technology firms to contribute when AI, automation, and robotics displace workers.

promises.question: What is your plan to make healthcare more affordable and accessible?
promises.answer: I will introduce an NJ 12 VA+ and Community Care Network pilot for U.S. citizens that expands access through existing VA facilities, staff, telehealth, purchasing systems, and existing civilian care/billing capacity. Veterans retain priority access, earned benefits, and VA-funded care. Civilian care funded through a dedicated civilian health fund and automated chargebacks, protecting separate veterans’ appropriations. The pilot will measure access/wait times (20 day/30 miles), medical debt, outcomes, provider capacity, and cost. Successful results can support a national VA+ expansion, proving that District First at-scale pilots work better than empty national promises.

promises.question: Do you support the war in Iran and federal defense spending? If not, what would you change?
promises.answer: The conflict in Iran is not a war by Congressional Record, but an unauthorized introduction of forces. I do not support military action without clear Article I authorization, defined objectives, and a diplomatic path. Congress must exercise its war powers rather than allow open-ended executive action. I support a capable defense, auditing Pentagon spending, and reducing contractor waste. Freed funds must be invested in healthcare, infrastructure, housing, and economic security in NJ 12. We must end the Bush-era preemptive war doctrine and return to global leadership on peace and human rights. The US has no military peer, and we must not squander American lives and resources on wealth extraction via armed conflict against non-peer nations.

promises.question: What are your thoughts about current immigration enforcement policies and what, if anything, would you do differently?
promises.answer: Congress has abrogated its constitutional responsibility for immigration policy, allowing the system to become a permanent political weapon. Democratic and Republican Administrations engineered this multi-decade crisis by understaffing immigration courts. Article II judges now carry nearly 6,000 pending cases each. Congress must fund enough judges and support staff to reduce active dockets to a manageable level, while stopping new filings from exceeding completions. That is the remedy for multiyear backlogs that push people out of compliance. I support civil enforcement, due process, family unity, fair hearings, and workable congressional rules, not militarized national policing or unconstitutional criminalization that bypasses federalism.

promises.question: What changes, if any, should Congress or the president make in elections (requiring voter ID, regulating mail-in voting, etc.)?
promises.answer: Voting must remain secure, accessible, and protected from political interference. States administer elections (Time, Manner and Place), and New Jersey should preserve early voting, mail-in voting (automatic/default), ballot tracking, secure ballot handling, secure drop boxes, and clear public communication about deadlines. Congress must protect voting rights, prevent partisan gerrymandering, strengthen election security, and ensure that every eligible voter can cast a ballot that is counted. Strengthen State rights and protections from federal interference.
